recipes.name: Risotto alla Milanese
recipes.flavorProfile: Golden, buttery and loose, with the honeyed, faintly bitter perfume of saffron and a rich savoury depth from the beef marrow and broth.
recipes.healthBenefit: A comforting rice dish that brings steady carbohydrate and some calcium from the cheese, though the butter and marrow make it a rich plate best eaten in a modest portion.

components.note: kept at a bare simmer, about 1 litre

ingredients.prepNote: carnaroli is the Milanese choice; vialone nano or arborio also work

ingredients.name: beef bone marrow
ingredients.prepNote: midollo, the mark of the Milanese version

ingredients.cutPrep: 1 small white onion, chopped almost to a paste
threads or powder, steeped in a ladle of hot broth

ingredients.prepNote: to taste, depending on the broth

instructions: Keep the broth at a bare simmer in a pot beside the stove. Steep the saffron in a small cup of the hot broth.
Melt half the butter with the chopped marrow in a wide, heavy pan over low heat until the marrow melts and turns translucent, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the onion and cook it very gently, stirring often, until soft and sweet without browning, 10 to 20 minutes.
Raise the heat a little, add the rice and toast it, stirring, until the grains are hot and glassy at the edges, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add a ladle of broth and stir until it is mostly absorbed. Keep adding broth a ladle at a time, stirring often, and pour in the saffron broth about halfway through.
Cook until the rice is tender with a slight bite and the risotto still runs a little when you tilt the pan, 16 to 18 minutes in all.
Take the pan off the heat, add the remaining butter and the Grana, and beat hard with a wooden spoon for a minute (the mantecatura). Rest 1 minute, season and serve at once, alone or beside ossobuco.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the risotto rice, which gives the dish its body.
From the Grana Padano beaten in at the end.

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's canonical butter, marrow and onion soffritto with carnaroli and meat broth, checked against the Scatti di Gusto and Linkiesta accounts (seen in search) that without marrow the dish is properly called risotto allo zafferano. No wine, as in the Dissapore version and many Milanese cooks; the brodo di carne base is served by the cup, so 1 litre is 4 servings.

recipes.name: Risotto ai Funghi Porcini
recipes.flavorProfile: Deep, woodsy and savoury, with creamy rice carrying the meaty chew of porcini and the earthy liquor they were soaked in.
recipes.healthBenefit: Dried porcini add fibre, B vitamins and minerals such as potassium and copper to a filling rice dish, finished with only a little butter and cheese.

components.note: hot, about 1 litre

ingredients.prepNote: carnaroli or arborio

ingredients.cutPrep: soaked 20 minutes in warm water, squeezed and roughly chopped
ingredients.prepNote: in autumn, 300 g fresh porcini sliced and sautéed are used instead
strained and added to the risotto
many cooks deglaze with it after toasting the rice
to taste

instructions: Soak the dried porcini in the warm water for 20 to 30 minutes. Lift them out, squeeze them and chop roughly, then strain the soaking water through a sieve lined with paper towel to catch the grit.
Warm the oil in a wide pan and cook the onion over low heat until soft and pale gold, 10 to 15 minutes.
Add the rice and toast it, stirring, for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine and let it evaporate.
Add the porcini and a couple of ladles of hot broth. Cook over medium heat, stirring often and adding broth and the strained soaking water a ladle at a time as each is absorbed.
When the rice is tender with a slight bite, 16 to 18 minutes, take it off the heat.
Beat in the cold butter and the Parmesan, scatter with parsley, rest 1 minute and serve.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the porcini, which are concentrated by drying.
From the mushrooms and their soaking liquor.

citations.source: Dissapore, Risotto ai funghi porcini secchi

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's dried porcini version with vegetable broth and the strained soaking water, with a splash of white wine added as most northern home cooks do. The brodo vegetale base is served by the cup, so 1 litre is 4.

recipes.name: Risi e Bisi
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet young peas in a loose, spoonable rice that sits halfway between risotto and soup, softly savoury with Parmigiano and a little parsley.
recipes.healthBenefit: Green peas bring plant protein, fibre, vitamin C and folate to the rice, making a gentle, filling spring bowl.

components.note: chicken and vegetable broth, about 2 litres, hot

ingredients.prepNote: fresh spring peas; the pods can be simmered and sieved into the broth
vialone nano is the Venetian rice

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

ingredients.prepNote: to taste

instructions: Keep the broth hot. Warm the oil in a wide pot with the sliced onion, parsley and peas and half a glass of water (about 100 ml).
Cook gently, covered, until the water has been absorbed and the peas are tender, 10 to 15 minutes. Do not brown the onion.
Season with salt, add the rice and stir for a minute.
Add hot broth so the rice is just covered, and keep topping it up as it is absorbed, stirring now and then, until the rice is al dente, 15 to 18 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the butter and Parmigiano. Add more broth until the rice is loose and slightly brothy, all'onda, grind over pepper and serve.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the half kilo of peas.
Green peas are a good source.

citations.source: Dissapore, Risi e bisi, la ricetta originale veneziana

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's Venetian version with no classic soffritto, peas stewed first with onion and parsley, and chicken and vegetable broth; search results (Saveur, Recipes from Italy) agree on vialone nano and a soupy finish served for San Marco on 25 April. Pancetta is an optional addition and left out here. Uses the existing Homemade Chicken Stock, 8 servings of 1 cup, for the 2 litres.

recipes.name: Gnocchi alla Sorrentina
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft potato gnocchi in a bright tomato and basil sauce, baked until the mozzarella melts into strings and the top blisters.
recipes.healthBenefit: Potatoes, tomato and mozzarella give carbohydrate, vitamin C, lycopene and calcium; the melted cheese makes it a hearty plate rather than a light one.

components.note: the whole batch, four plates
about 350 ml

ingredients.cutPrep: fior di latte, torn and drained

ingredients.prepNote: for the dish

instructions: Heat the oven to 450 °F (230 °C), or heat the grill to high. Warm the tomato sauce in a wide pan with half the basil.
Boil the gnocchi in plenty of salted water and lift them out as soon as they float, about 2 minutes.
Slide the gnocchi into the sauce and toss by shaking the pan rather than stirring, so they stay whole. Add about two thirds of the mozzarella.
Oil an ovenproof dish, or 4 small terracotta dishes, and fill with the gnocchi. Top with the rest of the mozzarella and the Parmesan.
Bake or grill until the cheese melts and browns in spots, 8 to 10 minutes. Scatter with the remaining basil and serve bubbling.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's method: gnocchi tossed in a short garlic, chili and basil tomato sauce with fior di latte, then browned under the grill in a terracotta dish, as in Sorrento. The sugo base stands in for the passata cooked with garlic. Uses the whole gnocchi base (4 plates); the sugo base gives 6 servings of 3/4 cup, so about 350 ml is 2 of them.

recipes.name: Gnocchi Burro e Salvia
recipes.flavorProfile: Pillowy potato gnocchi glossed in nutty melted butter with crisp, fragrant sage leaves and a snow of Parmigiano.
recipes.healthBenefit: Simple potato gnocchi give easy-going carbohydrate and some potassium; the butter sauce is rich, so a modest plate with a salad alongside suits it.

components.note: the whole batch, four plates

ingredients.prepNote: for the cooking water

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it.
Melt the butter slowly in a wide pan over low heat, add the sage leaves and let them sizzle until crisp and the butter smells nutty and turns pale gold, 3 to 4 minutes.
Drop the gnocchi into the boiling water and lift them out with a slotted spoon as soon as they float, 1 to 2 minutes.
Slide them into the butter with a spoonful of the cooking water and toss gently to coat.
Serve at once with a grating of nutmeg and the Parmesan.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the potato and flour in the gnocchi.

citations.source: Giallo Zafferano blog, Gnocchi burro e salvia

recipes.curationNote: Giallo Zafferano blog version (80 g butter, 12 sage leaves, nutmeg) compared with the Ricette dal Mondo proportions seen in search (100 g butter for 1 kg potatoes). Parmesan added as most northern cooks do. Uses the whole gnocchi base, 4 plates.

recipes.name: Polenta Concia
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick, stretchy mountain polenta with melted Fontina and Toma pulled through it, crowned with nutty brown butter.
recipes.healthBenefit: A warming alpine dish with protein and plenty of calcium from the cheese; with this much butter and Fontina it is a rich cold-weather meal, not an everyday one.

components.note: about 250 g coarse cornmeal cooked soft, a little over half the base batch

ingredients.name: Toma cheese
ingredients.prepNote: a young Toma is fine
browned

instructions: Cook the polenta for about 45 minutes, stirring often, until thick and pulling away from the sides of the pot.
While it cooks, take the rind off the Fontina and Toma and dice them. Grate the Grana.
Melt the butter in a small pan over low heat until it foams and turns golden brown and smells of hazelnut, 5 to 6 minutes.
In the last 5 minutes, stir the diced Fontina and Toma into the polenta until fully melted and stringy.
Spoon into warm terracotta bowls, pour the brown butter over each, and finish with Grana and pepper.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the Fontina, Toma and Grana.

citations.source: Dissapore, Polenta concia, la ricetta tipica valdostana

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's Valdostana version (250 g bramata polenta, 200 g Fontina, 100 g Toma, 100 g brown butter) checked against the Giallo Zafferano blog proportions seen in search (500 g, 250 g Fontina, 200 g Toma, 150 g butter for 6). The polenta base makes 4 plates from 400 g cornmeal, so 250 g here is 2.5 of its servings.

recipes.name: Canederli
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, savoury bread dumplings flecked with smoky speck, onion and herbs, floating in a clear, hot beef broth.
recipes.healthBenefit: A thrifty way to use stale bread that brings protein from the eggs, milk and speck; speck is cured and salty, so the broth needs little extra salt.

components.note: about 1.2 litres, hot, for serving

ingredients.baseName: Pain, baguette ou boule, de campagne
ingredients.cutPrep: stale white country bread, cut in small cubes
ingredients.prepNote: Knödelbrot in South Tyrol

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.prepNote: half for the dough, half for serving

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached
ingredients.prepNote: only as much as the dough needs to hold

instructions: Put the bread cubes in a bowl, pour over the warm milk and leave to soak for at least 30 minutes.
Melt the butter in a small pan and cook the onion and speck over low heat until the onion is soft, about 15 minutes. Let it cool.
Add the eggs, the onion and speck, the parsley and half the chives to the bread and knead by hand until it holds together. Add a spoonful of flour if it is wet, or a splash of milk if it is dry.
With wet hands, shape 12 balls about 6 cm across. Poach one first in gently bubbling salted water to check it holds, then cook the rest for 12 to 15 minutes.
Lift them out with a slotted spoon and serve 3 in each bowl with a ladle of hot broth and the remaining chives.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the eggs, milk and speck.

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's speck canederli in broth, compared with the alto-adige.com and austria.info accounts seen in search, which give 10 to 15 minutes' poaching and note that small ones go in beef broth and large ones beside sauerkraut. Cooking time lengthened from Dissapore's 5 minutes to the more usual 12 to 15. The brodo di carne base is served by the cup, so 1.2 litres is 5.

recipes.name: Gnudi
recipes.flavorProfile: Feather-light dumplings of ricotta and spinach, the filling of a ravioli without its pasta, bathed in sage butter and Parmigiano.
recipes.healthBenefit: Spinach brings folate, vitamin K and iron, and ricotta and egg add protein, in a dish with very little flour.

components.note: about 250 g, half the base batch, drained for several hours

ingredients.cutPrep: fresh, which boils down to about 250 g squeezed

ingredients.prepNote: 2 tablespoons for the dough, the rest for serving

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached
ingredients.prepNote: for rolling only

instructions: Drain the ricotta in a sieve for several hours, or overnight in the fridge if it is very wet.
Boil the spinach in a little salted water for 2 to 3 minutes, drain, cool and squeeze it hard until no more water comes out. Chop it finely.
Mix the ricotta, spinach, egg, 2 tablespoons of the Parmesan and the nutmeg with a fork and season with salt.
Shape into balls a little smaller than a walnut and roll each gently in flour.
Lower them into gently boiling salted water and lift them out as soon as they float, 1 to 3 minutes. Meanwhile melt the butter with the sage until it sizzles.
Toss the gnudi gently in the sage butter and serve with the rest of the Parmesan.

nutritionHighlights.note: Spinach is one of the richest greens.

citations.source: Visit Tuscany, La ricetta degli gnudi

recipes.curationNote: The Tuscan tourism board's recipe (250 g each ricotta and cooked spinach, one egg, nutmeg, flour for dusting, butter and sage), checked against several Giallo Zafferano blog versions seen in search that start from 500 g fresh spinach. The ricotta base makes about 500 g in 8 servings, so 250 g is 4 of them.

recipes.name: Risotto al Radicchio
recipes.flavorProfile: Creamy, wine-scented rice streaked purple with wilted Treviso radicchio, whose gentle bitterness is softened by butter and Grana.
recipes.healthBenefit: Radicchio adds vitamin K and plant polyphenols to the rice; the butter and cheese finish make it a moderately rich dish.

components.note: light and unsalted, about 1.2 litres, hot

ingredients.prepNote: vialone nano, carnaroli or arborio

ingredients.cutPrep: 3 heads radicchio di Treviso tardivo, cut in thin ribbons

ingredients.prepNote: or a small onion

ingredients.cutPrep: 60 g to start, 50 g cold to finish

ingredients.prepNote: a red Valpolicella is used by some Treviso cooks
to taste

instructions: Keep the broth hot. Melt 60 g butter in a wide, low pan and cook the shallot over low heat until translucent, 5 to 7 minutes.
Add the radicchio ribbons and cook, stirring, until wilted and soft, 5 minutes.
Add the rice, raise the heat and toast it until the grains crackle slightly, 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the wine and let it evaporate.
Lower to medium heat and add hot broth a ladle at a time, keeping the rice just covered and stirring often, for 16 to 18 minutes. Season as you go.
Off the heat, stir in the cold butter and Grana, cover and rest 2 minutes.
Beat the risotto hard with a spoon until creamy, grind over pepper and serve.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's Treviso-style method with radicchio tardivo wilted in butter before the rice, white wine and an unsalted vegetable broth, butter and Grana mantecatura. The brodo vegetale base is served by the cup, so 1.2 litres is 5.

recipes.name: Pizza Margherita
recipes.flavorProfile: A soft, blistered Neapolitan crust under sweet hand-crushed tomato, milky melted fior di latte, fresh basil and a thread of olive oil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Tomato brings lycopene and vitamin C and the mozzarella adds protein and calcium, in a pizza simple enough that one is a full meal rather than a treat piled high.

components.note: 4 dough balls of about 260 g

ingredients.cutPrep: San Marzano peeled tomatoes crushed by hand, about 100 g a pizza
ingredients.prepNote: seasoned with a pinch of salt

ingredients.cutPrep: fior di latte in strips, drained, about 80 g a pizza
a few leaves for each pizza

ingredients.prepNote: a tablespoon over each pizza
for the tomato

instructions: Put a baking steel or pizza stone on the highest shelf and heat the oven as hot as it goes, 500 to 550 °F (260 to 290 °C), for 45 to 60 minutes. Turn on the grill for the last 5 minutes.
Press one dough ball out from the centre with your fingertips, leaving a puffy rim of 1 to 2 cm, into a round about 30 cm across. Do not use a rolling pin.
Spread about 100 g crushed tomato in a spiral, leaving the rim bare. Scatter over a quarter of the mozzarella and a few basil leaves and pour over a spoon of oil.

Slide the pizza onto the hot stone and bake until the rim is puffed and spotted dark and the cheese has melted, 5 to 8 minutes in a home oven (60 to 90 seconds in a wood oven at 840 to 900 °F, 450 to 480 °C).
Finish with a fresh basil leaf and serve at once, then shape and bake the other three.

citations.source: Dissapore, Pizza napoletana fatta in casa

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's Verace Pizza Napoletana topping (about 100 g San Marzano and 80 g fior di latte per pizza, basil, oil, optional grated cheese) with home-oven times from the Scatti di Gusto and Linkiesta guides seen in search. Uses 4 of the pizza dough base's 6 balls.

recipes.name: Pizza Marinara
recipes.flavorProfile: The oldest tomato pizza of Naples: bright tomato, slivers of sweet baked garlic, dried oregano and plenty of green olive oil on a chewy, charred crust.
recipes.healthBenefit: With no cheese it is lighter than most pizzas and dairy-free, bringing lycopene from the tomato and monounsaturated fat from the olive oil.

components.note: 4 dough balls of about 260 g

instructions: Heat the oven with a stone or steel on the top shelf as hot as it goes, 500 to 550 °F (260 to 290 °C), for 45 to 60 minutes.
Stretch a dough ball by hand into a round about 30 cm across, leaving a raised rim.
Spread a quarter of the salted tomato in a spiral, leaving the rim bare. Scatter over the sliced garlic of one clove and a pinch of oregano.
Pour over a little oil in a spiral from the centre outwards.
Bake until the rim is puffed and charred in spots, 5 to 8 minutes in a home oven. Serve at once and repeat with the rest.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the extra virgin olive oil.

recipes.curationNote: The AVPN method (tomato in a spiral, thin garlic, a pinch of oregano, oil from the centre out, no cheese) as described on Wikipedia. Quantities per pizza follow the margherita. Uses 4 of the pizza dough base's 6 balls.

recipes.name: Focaccia Genovese
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin, golden and dimpled, with a crisp oiled base, a tender crumb and little pools of salty olive oil brine in every hollow.
recipes.healthBenefit: A plain bread made with extra virgin olive oil; it is salty and oily by design, so a piece with a meal or as a snack is the way it is eaten in Genoa.

components.note: the whole batch with its salamoia, one 30 x 40 cm tray

ingredients.cutPrep: for the tray and a last brushing
ingredients.prepNote: a Ligurian oil if you can find one

instructions: Oil a 30 x 40 cm metal tray well. Lay in the risen dough and stretch it gently towards the corners with oiled fingers. If it springs back, rest it 15 minutes and stretch again.
Leave it to rise in a warm place, about 82 to 86 °F (28 to 30 °C), until puffy, about 1 hour.

Whisk the salamoia from the dough recipe (its water, oil and salt) into a cloudy brine. Press deep dimples all over the dough with three fingers, right to the tray, and pour the brine over so it fills the holes.
Leave to rise again until the dimples have softened and swollen, 90 minutes to 2 1/2 hours. Heat the oven to 465 °F (240 °C).
Scatter with coarse salt and bake on the oven floor for 5 minutes, then on the middle shelf until golden, 9 to 12 minutes more.
Brush with a little more oil, lift onto a rack and eat warm or the same day.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the olive oil in and on the dough.

citations.source: Dissapore, Focaccia genovese, la ricetta e i trucchi per una fügassa perfetta

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's method (tray stretch, finger dimples, salamoia poured into the holes, long final rise, 240 °C bake), with the dough and its brine taken from the focaccia base, all 8 slices for one 30 x 40 cm tray; only extra oil for the tray and coarse salt are added here.

recipes.name: Focaccia Barese
recipes.flavorProfile: Tall, soft and crisp-edged, with a crumb kept tender by potato and durum wheat, topped with burst cherry tomatoes, black olives and oregano in a pool of oil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Tomatoes and olives bring vitamin C, lycopene and olive fats, and durum semola gives a little more protein than soft-wheat bread; the oiled tray makes it rich.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached
ingredients.prepNote: Italian 00 flour
Bari cooks often leave the stones in
generous, for the tin and the top

instructions: Mix the two flours, the mashed potato, the yeast and most of the water. Knead, adding the rest of the water and then the salt, until smooth and elastic, 10 to 12 minutes.
Cover and rest 30 minutes, then shape into a ball, seal in an oiled container and refrigerate 18 to 24 hours.
Bring the dough to room temperature and let it rise until almost tripled, 2 to 4 hours.
Pour 3 tablespoons of oil into a round 32 cm tin with sides at least 2 cm high. Lay in the dough and push it out to the edge with oiled fingers.
Press in the tomatoes, cut side down, and the olives. Season with salt and oregano and drizzle with the rest of the oil.
Bake in an oven heated as hot as it goes, 475 to 500 °F (245 to 260 °C), on the lowest shelf for 10 minutes, then on the top shelf until golden and crisp at the edge, 10 to 12 minutes more.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the wheat, durum semola and potato.

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's Bari dough of equal 00 flour and durum semola with mashed potato, cold-matured, in a round oiled tin topped with tomatoes, black olives and oregano; scaled from its three-tray quantities to one 32 cm tin, and malt left out as many home cooks do. Written from its ingredients rather than the general focaccia base, because the potato and semola dough is what makes it Barese.

recipes.name: Piadina Romagnola
recipes.flavorProfile: A soft, flaky flatbread, freckled brown from a dry hot pan and short with lard, folded warm around prosciutto, squacquerone or greens.
recipes.healthBenefit: A simple unleavened bread that gives carbohydrate for the day; the lard makes it short and rich, so what goes inside decides how light the meal is.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached
ingredients.prepNote: a soft, low-protein flour
strutto, the traditional fat

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.name: baking soda
ingredients.prepNote: about half a teaspoon

instructions: Mix the flour and baking soda in a bowl and rub in the lard with your fingertips until it disappears into the flour.
Add the salt, then pour in the milk and water little by little, kneading until the dough is smooth and firm, 8 to 10 minutes.
Wrap and rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Divide into 6 balls of about 150 g and roll each into a round 3 to 4 mm thick and about 25 cm across.
Heat a dry heavy pan or a testo until very hot. Cook each piadina 1 to 2 minutes a side, pricking the bubbles with a fork, until spotted brown.
Stack them under a cloth to keep soft, and fill while warm.

citations.source: Dissapore, Piadina romagnola, la ricetta perfetta

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's milk and water version with lard and bicarbonate, checked against Scatti di Gusto and the Giallo Zafferano blog in search (500 g flour, 90 to 100 g lard, 10 to 12 g salt, water only). Yeast left out, since the IGP piadina uses bicarbonate.

recipes.name: Ciabatta
recipes.flavorProfile: A flat, slipper-shaped loaf with a thin, crackling, flour-dusted crust and an open, glossy crumb full of large holes.
recipes.healthBenefit: A lean bread of flour, water, yeast and salt with only a little oil, good for sandwiches and soaking up sauces.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, wheat flour, white, bread flour
ingredients.cutPrep: 300 g for the biga, 200 g for the dough
ingredients.prepNote: a strong flour

ingredients.cutPrep: 150 ml cool for the biga, 230 ml for the dough
fresh, 1 g for the biga and 3 g for the dough

instructions: Make the biga the day before: mix 300 g flour, 150 ml cool water and 1 g yeast into a shaggy, fairly dry dough. Cover and leave at cool room temperature for 18 to 24 hours.

Break the biga into the remaining flour, add 3 g yeast and most of the remaining water and mix until smooth. Add the salt, then the last water little by little, and finally the oil, working until the dough is very soft, shiny and stretchy, 10 to 15 minutes.
Leave to rise in an oiled container for 3 hours, giving it a set of stretches and folds after the first and second hour.
Tip the dough onto a well floured surface, cut it into 2 or 3 rough rectangles and turn them onto floured parchment. Proof, uncovered or lightly covered, until puffy, 45 to 90 minutes.
Heat the oven with a tray or stone inside to 465 °F (240 °C). Slide in the loaves and bake until golden brown and hollow-sounding, 20 to 25 minutes.
Cool on a rack for at least 30 minutes before slicing.

citations.source: ChainBaker, How to make a 100% biga ciabatta

recipes.curationNote: A biga method from ChainBaker, with the hydration raised to the high (about 76 percent) level the Wikipedia history and the bakery recipes seen in search describe; ciabatta was first baked by Arnaldo Cavallari in Adria in 1982, which the region records.

recipes.name: Pane Toscano (Tuscan Saltless Bread)
recipes.flavorProfile: Plain, wheaty and unsalted, with a thick crackling crust and a firm, close crumb made to be eaten with salty salumi, rich stews and, once stale, in ribollita and panzanella.
recipes.healthBenefit: Made with no salt at all, it is a useful bread for anyone keeping sodium down, and it brings the slow carbohydrate of plain wheat.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached
ingredients.cutPrep: 125 g for the biga, 500 g for the dough
ingredients.prepNote: Italian type 0 flour

ingredients.cutPrep: 75 ml for the biga, about 300 ml for the dough
dry, a third of a teaspoon for the biga and a pinch for the dough
ingredients.prepNote: the DOP loaf uses a natural sourdough leaven instead

instructions: Make the biga: mix 125 g flour, 75 ml water and a third of a teaspoon of dry yeast, cover and leave at about 77 °F (25 °C) for 20 to 24 hours.
Mix the biga with the remaining flour, a pinch of yeast and about 300 ml water and knead until smooth and elastic, 10 to 12 minutes. No salt goes in.
Cover and rest for 30 to 45 minutes away from drafts.
Divide into two pieces of about 500 g and shape each into a long filone. Proof on a floured cloth, covered, until doubled, 2 to 3 hours.
Heat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Bake the loaves on a lined tray until the crust is deep gold and the base sounds hollow, 40 to 45 minutes.
Cool completely on a rack. Keep it in a cloth; it goes stale slowly, and stale is how much of Tuscan cooking wants it.

nutritionHighlights.note: There is none added, by tradition.

citations.source: Dissapore, Pane toscano fatto in casa, la ricetta perfetta

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's biga loaf, compared with the Gambero Rosso and Visit Tuscany accounts seen in search that the DOP pane toscano is made with type 0 flour, water and natural leaven and no salt.

recipes.name: Grissini Torinesi
recipes.flavorProfile: Long, knobbly, hand-stretched breadsticks, crisp right through and lightly nutty from olive oil and a dusting of durum semola.
recipes.healthBenefit: A dry, crunchy bread that keeps for days; a few sticks give some carbohydrate beside a meal or with antipasti.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.prepNote: the Turin bakers' fat; melted butter also works

instructions: Stir the yeast and sugar into the lukewarm water and leave until frothy, about 5 minutes.
Mix in the flour, lard and 2 tablespoons oil and knead for a few minutes, then add the salt and knead until smooth and elastic, 10 to 15 minutes.
Pat the dough into a long rectangle about 1 cm thick, brush with oil, dust with semola, cover and leave to rise until doubled, about 2 hours.
Heat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Cut the dough crosswise into strips about 1 cm wide.
Pick up each strip by both ends and stretch it, swinging gently, to the length of the tray. Lay them on lined trays a little apart.
Bake until golden and dry, 15 to 20 minutes. Cool completely so they crisp.

citations.source: Dissapore, I migliori pani italiani regione per regione (grissini stirati)

recipes.curationNote: Manu's Menu proportions and stretching method, with the butter replaced by lard as Dissapore's regional bread guide gives for grissini stirati (soft wheat, water, yeast, lard and salt). Salt raised from a quarter teaspoon to a usual bread level.

recipes.name: Calzone Napoletano
recipes.flavorProfile: A puffed half-moon of pizza dough, crisp outside, hiding hot, creamy ricotta with salame, melted fior di latte and black pepper, with a little tomato on top.
recipes.healthBenefit: Ricotta and mozzarella bring protein and calcium, but with salame and a whole folded pizza each it is a rich, filling meal.

components.note: 4 dough balls of about 260 g

ingredients.prepNote: ricotta di bufala if you can find it

ingredients.cutPrep: fior di latte, diced and drained

instructions: Heat the oven with a stone or tray inside to 475 °F (245 °C) for at least 30 minutes.
Mix the ricotta with the salame, Parmesan and pepper.
Stretch each dough ball into a round about 28 cm across. Spread a quarter of the ricotta over one half, leaving the edge clear, and scatter over a quarter of the mozzarella.
Fold the dough over into a half-moon and press the edge firmly closed with your fingers. Spread a spoonful of tomato over the top, drizzle with oil and make a small cut for steam.
Bake until puffed and deep golden, 12 to 18 minutes. Rest 2 minutes before cutting, as the filling is very hot.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the ricotta, mozzarella and salame.

citations.source: Giallo Zafferano blog, Calzone napoletano ricotta e salame

recipes.curationNote: The Neapolitan ricotta and salame filling from the Giallo Zafferano blog (which fries smaller calzoni), baked here as a pizzeria calzone with fior di latte, Parmesan and pepper as the Gambero Rosso and Lifestyle Blog versions seen in search do, with a little tomato on top. Uses 4 of the pizza dough base's 6 balls.

recipes.name: Sfincione Palermitano
recipes.flavorProfile: A tall, spongy Palermo pizza soaked with sweet onion and tomato sauce, studded with anchovies and caciocavallo and crusted with oregano breadcrumbs.
recipes.healthBenefit: Onions and tomato bring vitamin C and fibre and the anchovies add omega-3 fats, in a bread rich with oil and cheese and best shared in squares.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.cutPrep: for the dough, the sauce, the tin and the top
6 to 8 fillets in oil, broken up

ingredients.name: caciocavallo cheese
ingredients.cutPrep: two thirds cubed, one third grated
ingredients.prepNote: a young, semi-aged caciocavallo

ingredients.name: dry breadcrumbs
ingredients.cutPrep: mixed with oregano and a little oil

instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the water. Mix with the flour, semola and 2 tablespoons of oil, then add the salt and knead into a soft, sticky dough, 10 minutes. Cover and let rise until doubled, 2 to 3 hours.

Meanwhile, stew the onions gently in 4 tablespoons of oil with a splash of water until very soft, 15 to 20 minutes. Add the passata, a pinch of salt and oregano and simmer until thick, 20 to 30 minutes.
Oil a 30 x 40 cm tray well and push the dough into it with oiled fingers. Press the anchovy pieces and cubed caciocavallo into the dough.
Spread the onion and tomato sauce over the top, then the grated caciocavallo, then the breadcrumbs mixed with oregano and oil. Leave to rise 1 hour.
Bake at 480 °F (250 °C) until the base is golden and the top crusted, 25 to 30 minutes. Serve warm or at room temperature in squares.

citations.source: Dissapore, Sfincione palermitano, la ricetta originale

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's Palermo sfincione (soft wheat and semola dough, onion and passata sauce, anchovies, caciocavallo and breadcrumbs, 250 °C for 30 minutes), compared with the Scatti di Gusto and Giallo Zafferano blog versions seen in search; the sauce is cooked longer, as most Palermitan cooks do. The white Bagheria version is a different dish.

recipes.name: Taralli Pugliesi
recipes.flavorProfile: Little crunchy rings, short and crumbly from white wine and olive oil, scented with fennel seed and boiled before baking for their glossy, snapping crust.
recipes.healthBenefit: Made with olive oil rather than butter, they bring monounsaturated fat; they are a dense snack, so a handful with wine or olives is plenty.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached
ingredients.prepNote: Italian type 0 flour
plus a handful for the boiling water
or black pepper or chili flakes

instructions: Mix the flour, salt and fennel seed, then work in the oil and wine and knead until smooth, firm and no longer greasy, about 10 minutes. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Pinch off small pieces, roll each into a rope about the thickness of a pencil and 8 cm long, and close it into a ring, pressing the ends together.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Drop in the taralli a few at a time and lift them out as soon as they float, 1 to 2 minutes.
Spread them on a clean cloth to dry for at least 2 hours.
Bake on lined trays at 375 °F (190 °C) until golden, 15 to 25 minutes, then leave them in the switched-off oven, door ajar, to dry further as it cools. Store airtight.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the extra virgin olive oil.

citations.source: Scatti di Gusto, Taralli pugliesi, ricetta originale

recipes.curationNote: Scatti di Gusto's quantities (550 g flour, 180 g wine, 130 g oil, 12 g salt), with fennel seed from the 1 kg and tarallini versions seen in search. Boiled before baking, as Apulian bakers do. Shelved as a snack type on the Pizza & Breads shelf.

recipes.name: Panzerotti Pugliesi
recipes.flavorProfile: Small half-moons of soft dough fried until blistered and golden, bursting with molten mozzarella and oregano-scented tomato.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mozzarella brings protein and calcium, but deep-fried in oil these are a street-food treat rather than an everyday meal.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached
ingredients.prepNote: 00 flour

ingredients.baseName: Grains, wheat flour, white, bread flour
ingredients.prepNote: a strong Manitoba-style flour

ingredients.cutPrep: for the dough and the filling
fior di latte, diced and drained well

ingredients.name: peanut or sunflower oil for deep frying
ingredients.prepNote: about 60 ml is taken up by the dough

instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the water. Mix in both flours and 1 tablespoon of oil, then the salt, and knead until smooth, 10 minutes. Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1 1/2 hours.
Divide into 10 balls, space them apart under a cloth and let them rise 30 minutes more.
Season the passata with oregano, salt and the remaining oil. Mix the drained mozzarella with it just before filling.
Roll each ball into a thin round about 14 cm across. Spoon filling on one half, fold over and press the edge hard with a fork so it is fully sealed.
Heat the frying oil to 340 to 350 °F (170 to 175 °C). Fry 2 or 3 at a time, turning, until puffed and deep golden, 2 to 4 minutes. Drain on paper and eat hot.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's Apulian fried panzerotti (00 and Manitoba dough, fior di latte and passata with oregano, 10 pieces), with frying temperature and time added from usual practice since the page gives none. The frying oil is listed as not counted, as only part of it is absorbed.

recipes.name: Cacciucco alla Livornese
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick, peppery tomato and red wine stew of octopus, cuttlefish, rockfish, prawns and mussels, ladled over garlic-rubbed toast that drinks up the broth.
recipes.healthBenefit: Many kinds of fish and shellfish together bring lean protein, iodine, selenium, vitamin B12 and omega-3 fats, with lycopene from the tomato.

components.note: about 1 litre, hot, added a ladle at a time
the whole loaf, 16 slices, toasted and rubbed with garlic, two or three to a bowl

ingredients.cutPrep: cuttlefish and squid, cleaned, in strips
monkfish or other firm rockfish fillet, in chunks
ingredients.prepNote: Livorno uses scorpionfish, gurnard and dogfish as the catch allows

ingredients.name: scorpionfish, gurnard or dogfish (palombo) in pieces
ingredients.prepNote: heads and bones go into the stock

ingredients.cutPrep: prawns or mantis shrimp, in the shell
about 600 g in the shell, scrubbed and debearded
ingredients.prepNote: weight given is the meat

ingredients.cutPrep: loosened with a ladle of stock

ingredients.prepNote: Visit Tuscany uses white

ingredients.cutPrep: 4 cloves crushed, plus 2 for rubbing the toast

ingredients.prepNote: plus a drizzle to serve
to taste

instructions: In a wide, heavy pot, warm the oil and gently fry the crushed garlic, onion, sage and chile until soft and fragrant, 5 to 8 minutes.
Add the octopus and cuttlefish and cook, stirring, for 3 to 5 minutes. Pour in the wine and let it bubble off for 2 to 3 minutes.

Add the tomatoes and the tomato paste loosened with a ladle of hot stock. Season with salt, add another ladle of stock, partly cover and simmer gently until the octopus is nearly tender, 40 to 50 minutes, adding stock as it thickens.

Add the rockfish and monkfish and simmer 8 to 10 minutes. Add the prawns with a ladle of stock and cook 6 to 8 minutes, then add the mussels and parsley and cook until the shells open, 5 to 7 minutes. Discard any that stay shut.
Meanwhile toast the bread in the oven at 350 °F (180 °C), 6 to 10 minutes, turning once, and rub each slice with a cut garlic clove.

Lay two or three slices in each warm bowl. Ladle over the octopus and cuttlefish first, then the fish, then the prawns and mussels and plenty of broth. Finish with black pepper and a thread of oil and serve very hot.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the octopus, fish and shellfish.
From the octopus, mussels and fish.

citations.source: Dissapore, Cacciucco alla livornese, la ricetta della Trattoria Galileo
Visit Tuscany, La ricetta del cacciucco alla livornese

recipes.curationNote: Trattoria Galileo's version on Dissapore (red wine, octopus and cuttlefish first, fish, then shellfish, three toasts a bowl) compared with Visit Tuscany's (white wine, 2 dl oil, sage and chile soffritto, a thick broth of fish heads). The mixed rockfish are split between monkfish, which the database holds, and the rest listed as not counted. The fumetto base gives 6 servings of 1 cup, so about 1 litre is 4 of them; the toast is the whole 16-slice loaf of the Pane Toscano recipe in this file.

recipes.name: Branzino al Forno con Patate
recipes.flavorProfile: Whole sea bass baked on a bed of thin potato slices, its flesh moist and sweet, scented with garlic, bay, thyme and lemon, the potatoes crisp at the edges and soft beneath.
recipes.healthBenefit: Sea bass is lean protein with omega-3 fats, vitamin D and selenium, and the potatoes add potassium and vitamin C in a simple one-tray meal.

ingredients.cutPrep: 2 whole branzino of about 800 g, scaled and gutted
ingredients.prepNote: weight given is the edible flesh, about half the whole fish

ingredients.cutPrep: yellow-fleshed, peeled and sliced 5 mm thick

instructions: Heat the oven to 350 °F (180 °C), without fan if you can.
Rinse the fish inside and out and pat dry. Put a garlic clove, two bay leaves, two lemon slices and a pinch of salt inside each.
Toss the potato slices with the oil, salt, pepper and thyme until coated, and spread them in one layer in a large, heavy baking dish.
Lay the fish on the potatoes, season the skin with a pinch of salt, add the rest of the lemon slices and drizzle with a little more oil. Make two shallow cuts in the skin of each.
Bake until the flesh at the backbone is white and flakes, 35 to 45 minutes.
Fillet the fish at the table and serve with the potatoes and the juices from the dish.

citations.source: Dissapore, Branzino al forno con patate

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's method (bay, garlic and lemon inside, potatoes tossed with oil and thyme, 180 °C for 40 minutes) compared with the oven acqua pazza versions on Dissapore, which bake a whole fish at 220 °C for 25 minutes. Fish weight entered as edible flesh so the nutrients are not read from bones and head.

recipes.name: Baccalà alla Vicentina
recipes.flavorProfile: Stockfish baked very slowly in milk and olive oil with onion and anchovy until it is soft, silky and savoury under a golden crust of Grana, served with yellow polenta.
recipes.healthBenefit: Dried cod is concentrated lean protein with iodine and vitamin B12; the slow bake in oil and milk makes it rich, so a modest plate with polenta is the custom.

components.note: the whole batch of soft or grilled polenta, one plate each

ingredients.name: stockfish (stoccafisso), soaked
ingredients.cutPrep: soaked at least 48 hours, water changed every 4 hours, in pieces
ingredients.prepNote: Vicenza uses air-dried, unsalted cod and still calls it baccalà

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D
Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.prepNote: little, as the anchovies are salty

instructions: Warm a little of the oil in a pan and melt the anchovies in it. Add the onion and cook gently until soft and pale gold, about 10 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the parsley.
Pat the soaked stockfish dry and dust the pieces lightly with flour, shaking off the excess.
Spread some of the onion over the base of a snug baking dish, lay the fish on it side by side and cover with the rest of the onion.
Pour over the remaining oil and the milk, which should just cover the fish. Season with very little salt, plenty of pepper and the Grana.
Cover with foil and bake at 340 °F (170 °C) for 1 hour, then uncover and bake until the liquid has nearly gone and a golden crust forms, 30 to 40 minutes more.
Best made a day ahead and reheated gently. Serve hot with the polenta.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the stockfish, which is not counted, and the anchovies and Grana, which are.

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's Vicenza method (anchovy and onion soffritto, floured stockfish, oil and milk to the level of the fish, Grana, 170 °C for 1 hour covered then 30 minutes uncovered), which matches the Venerabile Confraternita del Bacalà's method as commonly quoted: slow cooking, milk and oil, polenta alongside. The original simmers on the stove for over 4 hours; the oven version is given. Stockfish is not in the database, so it is listed as not counted. The polenta base gives 4 plates, all used here.

recipes.name: Fritto Misto di Mare
recipes.flavorProfile: Prawns, squid rings, small red mullet, anchovies and pieces of cod in the thinnest crisp coat of semola and rice flour, salted hot and eaten with lemon.
recipes.healthBenefit: The mixed seafood brings protein, iodine, selenium and omega-3 fats from the oily fish; deep-fried, it is a treat for a seaside lunch rather than an everyday plate.

ingredients.cutPrep: 12 fresh anchovies, heads off and gutted
4 small red mullet, heads off and gutted
1 large squid, cleaned, body in rings, tentacles whole

ingredients.name: seed oil for deep frying (peanut or sunflower)
ingredients.prepNote: only a small part is taken up
to salt after frying

instructions: Clean all the seafood, rinse it and dry it very well with kitchen paper; wet fish spits and goes soggy.
Mix the semola and rice flour in a bowl. Heat the oil in a deep pan to 340 to 350 °F (170 to 175 °C).
Dredge a few pieces at a time, shaking off the excess flour, and fry in small batches: squid and prawns 1 to 2 minutes, anchovies 2 minutes, mullet and cod 3 to 4 minutes, until pale gold and crisp.
Lift out with a slotted spoon onto paper and keep each batch warm while you fry the rest.
Salt over the top and serve at once with lemon wedges.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the prawns, squid and fish.
From the anchovies and red mullet.

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's mixture (12 prawns, 12 anchovies, 4 red mullet, 300 g cod, 1 squid) and its semola and rice flour dredge, which is the light Italian coat with no batter. The page gives no oil temperature or times; usual frying values were added. The frying oil is listed as not counted.

recipes.name: Impepata di Cozze
recipes.flavorProfile: A pot of mussels steamed open in their sea juices with a heavy hand of black pepper, finished with parsley and lemon, for mopping with bread.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mussels are a rich source of vitamin B12, iron, selenium and protein, cooked with no added fat at all.

ingredients.cutPrep: 1.5 kg in the shell, scrubbed and debearded
ingredients.prepNote: weight given is the meat
be generous

ingredients.cutPrep: coarse, for the soaking water only
ingredients.prepNote: most is poured away

instructions: Soak the mussels in cold water with the coarse salt for at least 1 hour.
Throw away any broken or gaping mussels that do not close when tapped. Scrub the shells, pull off the beards and rinse well.
Put the mussels in a wide pot with plenty of black pepper. Cover and cook over high heat, shaking the pot, until most have opened, 4 to 6 minutes.
Discard any that stay closed. Squeeze over the lemon, scatter with parsley and serve at once in bowls with the juices and toasted bread.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's Neapolitan impepata: mussels, pepper, parsley and lemon only, no oil, no garlic, no wine, cooked by their liquid. Mussel weight entered as meat (about a quarter of shell weight).

recipes.name: Calamari Ripieni al Sugo
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender whole squid packed with a savoury filling of their chopped tentacles, anchovy, garlic, parsley and breadcrumbs, simmered in a basil tomato sauce with a little chile.
recipes.healthBenefit: Squid is lean protein with vitamin B12, copper and selenium, and the tomato sauce brings lycopene and vitamin C.

ingredients.cutPrep: 8 medium squid, cleaned, bodies whole, tentacles and fins chopped

ingredients.name: dry breadcrumbs
ingredients.prepNote: enough to make the filling hold

ingredients.cutPrep: 2 cloves, one chopped for the filling, one crushed for the sauce

instructions: Clean the squid: pull out the quill, ink sac, beak and eyes. Keep the bodies whole and chop the tentacles, fins and heads.
Mix the chopped squid with the egg, broken anchovies, chopped garlic, parsley, salt and pepper, and add breadcrumbs until it holds together.
Fill the bodies about three quarters full, as they shrink, and close each with a toothpick.
Brown the squid in the oil with the crushed garlic, about 2 minutes a side.
Add the passata, basil, chile and a pinch of salt. Cover and simmer gently until the squid are tender, 25 to 40 minutes, adding a splash of hot water if the sauce gets too thick.
Remove the toothpicks and serve with the sauce, with bread, rice or polenta.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's filling of the squid's chopped tentacles, egg, anchovies, garlic, parsley and breadcrumbs, browned and then simmered in passata with basil and chile. Simmering time stretched from its minimum of 20 minutes to a range, since larger squid need longer to turn tender.

recipes.name: Pesce Spada alla Ghiotta (Sicilian Swordfish)
recipes.flavorProfile: Meaty chunks of swordfish finished in a sweet-sour tomato sauce of onion, celery, green olives and capers, bright with oregano and parsley.
recipes.healthBenefit: Swordfish is rich in protein, selenium and vitamin D, and the tomato sauce adds vitamin C and lycopene; swordfish carries more mercury than small fish, so it suits an occasional meal and is best skipped in pregnancy.

ingredients.cutPrep: 2 thick steaks, skin and dark parts removed, in large cubes

instructions: Sear the swordfish cubes in 1 tablespoon of the oil over high heat, turning, until browned on all sides, 2 to 3 minutes. Set aside.
In a wide pan with the rest of the oil and a splash of water, soften the onion and celery over low heat, 8 to 10 minutes. Add the chile, capers and olives and cook 2 minutes.
Add the tomato and salt and simmer gently for 10 to 15 minutes.
Return the swordfish to the sauce and cook until just done through, 5 to 10 minutes depending on size. Do not let it overcook or it turns dry.
Finish with oregano and parsley, turn off the heat and serve hot with bread.

citations.source: Giallo Zafferano blog (Pelle di Pollo), Pesce spada alla ghiotta
Scatti di Gusto, Braciole di pesce spada alla messinese
U.S. FDA, Advice about eating fish

recipes.curationNote: The Messina ghiotta (onion, celery, green olives, capers, tomato) from the Pelle di Pollo blog, doubled from 2 to 4 servings, compared with the ghiotta variant on Scatti di Gusto's Messina braciole page. The database holds swordfish only as a poached row, used here for the fish itself. Mercury note from FDA fish advice.

recipes.name: Sarde a Beccafico (Catanese)
recipes.flavorProfile: Pairs of vinegar-cured fresh sardines sandwiched around a pecorino, garlic and parsley filling, then crumbed and fried golden, good hot or cold.
recipes.healthBenefit: Sardines are among the richest sources of omega-3 fats, vitamin D, vitamin B12 and calcium; fried and filled with cheese, they make a hearty dish.

ingredients.cutPrep: 1 kg fresh sardines, heads and backbones removed, opened flat
ingredients.prepNote: weight given is after cleaning

ingredients.cutPrep: strong red wine vinegar, to cover
ingredients.prepNote: mostly poured away

ingredients.cutPrep: 3 for the filling, 2 for coating, beaten

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.cutPrep: absorbed from about 700 ml used for frying
ingredients.prepNote: Catania fries in olive oil

instructions: Lay the opened sardines in a dish, cover completely with vinegar and leave until the flesh turns white, 20 to 30 minutes and no longer, or they fall apart. Drain and pat dry.
Beat 3 eggs with salt and pepper and mix in the garlic, parsley, breadcrumbs and pecorino. Shape into small flat ovals, thinner at the edges.
Lay a filling oval on one opened sardine, skin side down, and cover with a second sardine, skin side up, pressing the edges together.
Dip each pair in the 2 remaining beaten eggs, then in flour, coating the sides too.
Fry in hot olive oil at about 340 °F (170 °C), turning once, until golden, 2 to 4 minutes. Drain on paper, salt lightly and serve hot or cold.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore gives the Catania version: vinegar-cured sardines paired around a pecorino, egg and breadcrumb filling, egged, floured and fried. The Palermo version (baked rolls with raisins, pine nuts, orange and bay) is a different preparation. Servings not given by the source; 1 kg of sardines set at 6. Frying oil entered as the share taken up.

recipes.name: Polpo e Patate
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender, slightly sweet octopus and soft boiled potato tossed warm with olive oil, lemon, garlic and parsley.
recipes.healthBenefit: Octopus is lean protein with plenty of vitamin B12, iron and selenium, and the potatoes and parsley add potassium and vitamin C.

ingredients.prepNote: frozen and thawed is more tender

ingredients.cutPrep: 2 cloves, one whole for the pot, one finely chopped

instructions: Rinse the octopus. Put it in a wide pan with a glass of water, the bay leaves, the whole garlic clove and a little salt and pepper. Cover and cook over low heat until a fork slides in easily, 20 to 45 minutes from the boil depending on size.
Leave the octopus to cool completely in its liquid, 1 1/2 to 2 hours; this keeps it tender.
Meanwhile boil the potato chunks in salted water until just tender, 10 to 15 minutes. Drain and cool a little.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, chopped garlic and parsley into a dressing.
Cut the octopus into pieces, toss with the potatoes and the dressing and serve warm or at room temperature.

citations.source: Dissapore, Insalata di polpo con patate

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore's method: octopus cooked covered in a glass of water with bay and garlic and cooled in its liquid, potatoes boiled apart, then dressed with oil, lemon, garlic and parsley, which matches the Apulian versions seen in search that boil the two separately. Cooking time widened for a larger octopus.

recipes.name: Pesce all'Acqua Pazza
recipes.flavorProfile: Whole sea bass poached in a light, brothy splash of water and white wine with burst cherry tomatoes, garlic, chile and parsley, delicate and clean-tasting.
recipes.healthBenefit: Gently poached fish keeps its protein, omega-3 fats and vitamin D with only a little oil, and the tomatoes add vitamin C and lycopene.

ingredients.cutPrep: 2 whole spigola of about 700 g, scaled and gutted
ingredients.prepNote: weight given is the edible flesh; orata (sea bream) is the other usual fish
pomodorini del piennolo if you can find them

ingredients.cutPrep: a bunch, leaves chopped, stalks for the fish
dry, such as Greco di Tufo

instructions: Rinse the fish well, especially the belly. Tuck half a garlic clove, a pinch of salt and some parsley stalks inside each.
In a wide pan that holds both fish, warm the oil with the remaining garlic and the chile for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes and cook until they start to soften, 3 to 4 minutes.
Lay in the fish, pour over the wine and water so there is about 1.5 cm of liquid, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and poach over low heat, spooning the liquid over now and then, until the flesh at the backbone flakes, 15 to 25 minutes. (In the oven, bake uncovered at 425 °F, 220 °C, for 20 to 25 minutes.)

Lift out the fish, remove skin and bones and lay the fillets on warm plates. Reduce the liquid for a minute or two, taste for salt, and spoon it with the tomatoes over the fish. Scatter with chopped parsley.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the cherry tomatoes and parsley.

citations.source: Dissapore, Orata all'acqua pazza, la ricetta napoletana

recipes.curationNote: Both Dissapore versions compared: the spigola poached on the stove in water, Greco di Tufo, piennolo tomatoes, garlic, chile and parsley, and the orata baked at 220 °C with half a glass each of water and wine. Sea bass is used, since sea bream is not in the database; the stove method is given with the oven as an alternative. Fish weight entered as edible flesh.

components.note: about 1 litre, hot, added a ladle at a time
the whole batch, scattered over in the last 5 minutes

recipes.name: Ossobuco alla Milanese
recipes.flavorProfile: Veal shank braised in white wine and broth until it falls from the bone, with a buttery, glossy sauce and a bright lift of lemon, garlic and parsley scattered over at the end, and the marrow to scoop from the middle.
recipes.healthBenefit: The veal brings protein, zinc and vitamin B12, and the long braise draws collagen from the shank into the sauce; the marrow makes it a rich dish.

ingredients.cutPrep: 4 crosscut shanks 3 to 4 cm thick, about 1.4 kg with bone
ingredients.prepNote: weight given is the meat

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Cut two or three small nicks through the skin round each shank so it does not curl, then dust both cut faces lightly with flour.
Melt the butter with the oil in a wide, heavy pan that holds the shanks in one layer. Brown them over medium-high heat, 3 to 4 minutes a side, and lift them out.
Lower the heat, add the onion, carrot and celery with the sage and rosemary, and cook gently until soft, 8 to 10 minutes.
Return the shanks, pour in the wine and let it bubble until the smell of alcohol is gone, 2 to 3 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

Add hot broth to come halfway up the meat, cover and simmer very gently for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, turning the shanks once and adding broth a ladle at a time as it reduces. Handle them carefully so the marrow stays in.

When the meat comes away from the bone, uncover and let the sauce thicken for a few minutes. Scatter the gremolata over, cover for 5 minutes, and serve with the sauce, traditionally beside risotto alla milanese.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the veal and the marrow.

citations.source: Giallo Zafferano blog (Inventaricette), Ossobuco alla milanese

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (4 shanks, flour, butter, soffritto, white wine, 1 litre broth, sage and rosemary, about 1 h 30) and Inventaricette (shanks 3 to 4 cm, 50 g butter, broth, 90 to 120 minutes, gremolada of lemon zest, garlic and parsley added 5 minutes before the end) agree closely. The tomato some add is left out, as the Milanese in bianco version is the older one. Gremolata points at the base; meat weight is entered without bone.

recipes.name: Saltimbocca alla Romana
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin veal slices with a leaf of sage and a sheet of prosciutto pinned on top, seared in butter in a couple of minutes and finished with a quick white wine sauce that is salty, herby and buttery.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean veal gives protein, niacin and vitamin B12; the prosciutto adds a good deal of salt, so no extra salt goes in.

ingredients.cutPrep: 8 thin slices of topside, lightly pounded

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Pound the veal slices between two sheets of baking paper until thin and even.
Lay a slice of prosciutto and a sage leaf on each and pin them in place with a toothpick. Dust the underside lightly with flour if you like.
Melt most of the butter in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Cook the saltimbocca prosciutto side down first for about 1 minute, then turn and cook 1 to 2 minutes more.
Lift them onto a warm plate. Pour the wine into the pan, scrape up the browned bits and let it reduce by half, 2 to 3 minutes, then swirl in the last of the butter.
Spoon the sauce over the veal, add a grind of pepper and serve at once. Taste before salting: the ham usually brings enough.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (4 slices, 50 g butter, 150 ml wine, 1 to 2 minutes a side, flour optional) and Misya (30 g butter, 8 sage leaves, about 2 minutes a side) compared; eight smaller slices for four people as Misya does. Prosciutto entered as cured ham, the same food.

recipes.name: Pollo alla Cacciatora
recipes.flavorProfile: Chicken pieces browned and braised with soffritto, white wine, rosemary and a little tomato until the meat is tender and the sauce clings, savoury and herby with a gentle sweetness from the carrot and pepper.
recipes.healthBenefit: The chicken gives protein, niacin and selenium, and the vegetables and tomato add vitamin C, potassium and lycopene.

ingredients.cutPrep: 1 chicken of about 1.4 kg in 8 pieces, skin on
ingredients.prepNote: weight given is the meat with skin, without bone
or 300 g peeled tomatoes; leave out for the in bianco version

instructions: Pat the chicken pieces dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pan and brown the chicken well on all sides over medium-high heat, 8 to 10 minutes. Lift it out.
In the same pan cook the onion, carrot, celery, pepper and garlic gently with the rosemary until soft, about 15 minutes.
Return the chicken, pour in the wine and let it bubble off, 2 to 3 minutes. Add the tomatoes.
Cover and braise over low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, turning the pieces now and then and adding a splash of hot water if it looks dry.
Uncover, add the olives if using, and cook 5 to 10 minutes more until the sauce thickens and the thigh juices run clear. Serve with bread or polenta.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore gives the in bianco version (whole chicken, 4 carrots, celery, onion, garlic, green pepper, rosemary, half a glass of white wine, soffritto 15 minutes, braise 20 to 25 then 5 uncovered, optional olives); Misya adds cherry tomatoes and pancetta. Kept Dissapore with the Misya tomatoes as an optional line, and left out pancetta. Chicken entered without bone.

recipes.name: Bistecca alla Fiorentina
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick T-bone seared hard over embers so the outside is charred and salty and the inside stays rare and juicy, finished only with coarse salt, pepper and a thread of olive oil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef is rich in protein, iron, zinc and vitamin B12; it is a large cut of red meat best shared and eaten with vegetables.

ingredients.cutPrep: 1 T-bone 4 to 5 cm thick, about 1.4 kg with bone, at room temperature
ingredients.prepNote: weight given is the meat without bone

instructions: Take the steak out of the fridge 2 to 3 hours before cooking so it reaches room temperature. Do not salt or oil it.
Build a hot charcoal fire with a bed of glowing embers and no flame, or heat a grill to 480 °F (250 °C) or more.
Lay the steak on the grill about 10 cm from the embers and cook 3 to 5 minutes, without moving it, until a dark crust forms. Turn it once and cook the second side 3 to 5 minutes.
Stand the steak upright on its bone for 2 to 3 minutes so the heat runs through the bone. The center should read 122 to 131 °F (50 to 55 °C): it is served rare.
Rest it 5 to 10 minutes, then carve the fillet and sirloin off the bone and slice. Season only now with coarse salt, pepper and a little oil.

citations.source: Giallo Zafferano blog (Il caldo sapore del sud), Bistecca alla fiorentina
Visit Italy, Come preparare la bistecca alla fiorentina

recipes.curationNote: Both sources: Chianina T-bone 3 to 5 cm, room temperature, very hot grill, 3 to 4 minutes a side, 2 to 3 minutes on the bone, core 50 to 55 °C, salt only after. Meat entered without bone, as for the fish.

recipes.name: Cotoletta alla Milanese
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick bone-in veal rib chop in a crisp golden crust of egg and breadcrumbs, fried slowly in clarified butter so it stays pink and juicy inside, with only salt and lemon to finish.
recipes.healthBenefit: The veal gives protein, niacin and vitamin B12; fried in butter it is a rich dish best eaten with a salad.

ingredients.cutPrep: 4 rib chops about 2.5 cm thick, 250 g each with bone, fat trimmed
ingredients.prepNote: weight given is the meat without bone

ingredients.name: dry breadcrumbs
ingredients.cutPrep: fine, made from stale white bread

ingredients.prepNote: the share taken up; fry in about 250 g

instructions: Trim the fat from the chops and nick the edges so they stay flat. Pound the meat lightly to an even thickness, leaving the bone.
Dip each chop in beaten egg and press it into the breadcrumbs. Dip it again in egg and again in crumbs, pressing well so the crust holds.
Melt the clarified butter in a wide pan to about 1 cm deep over medium heat. It is ready when a crumb sizzles at once.
Fry the chops 4 to 6 minutes a side, until the crust is deep gold and the meat is still pink at the bone. Keep the heat steady so the butter does not burn.
Drain on paper, salt only now, and serve with lemon wedges.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (4 bone-in rib chops, 4 eggs, 300 g crumbs, 300 g clarified butter, double coat, 5 minutes a side, salt after) and Misya (4 chops of 250 g, 200 g clarified butter, 2 eggs) agree on the method. Kept the double coat and salt after. Frying fat entered as the share absorbed; breadcrumbs are not in the database.

recipes.name: Brasato al Barolo
recipes.flavorProfile: Beef marinated overnight in Barolo with vegetables and warm spices, then braised for hours until it slices like butter, served in a dark, velvety wine sauce made from the blended vegetables.
recipes.healthBenefit: The beef gives protein, iron, zinc and vitamin B12; most of the alcohol cooks off over the long braise, though some remains.

ingredients.cutPrep: one piece of eye of round (girello) or shoulder, tied

ingredients.baseName: Alcoholic beverage, spirit, ~40% v/v, all (Brandy, Gin, Rum, Vodka and Whisky)
ingredients.prepNote: optional

instructions: Put the beef in a snug bowl with the vegetables, garlic, herbs and spices and pour over the whole bottle of wine. Cover and leave in the fridge 8 to 12 hours, turning it once or twice.
Lift out the meat and pat it dry. Strain the marinade, keeping the wine and the vegetables apart.
Brown the beef all over in the butter and oil in a heavy casserole, 8 to 10 minutes. Pour in the brandy if using and let it bubble off.
Add the drained vegetables and stir for 5 minutes, then pour in the wine and season with salt. Bring to a bare simmer.
Cover and cook over the lowest heat for 3 to 4 hours, turning the meat now and then, until a fork slides in easily.

Lift out the meat and rest it 10 minutes. Remove the herbs and blend the vegetables with the cooking liquid into a smooth sauce, reducing it a little if thin. Slice the beef and serve with the sauce and polenta or mashed potatoes.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (1 kg beef, vegetables, herb bundle, cinnamon, nutmeg, pepper, whole bottle of Barolo, butter, brandy, marinate 8 to 12 h, 4 h very low heat, sauce blended) and Misya (1.2 kg girello for 6, about 2 h). Kept the long Dissapore braise with the Misya amount for six. Barolo entered as red wine.

recipes.name: Porchetta
recipes.flavorProfile: Pork belly rolled round a tenderloin with garlic, rosemary, sage, fennel and plenty of pepper, slow-roasted until the inside is moist and fragrant and the skin shatters like glass.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork gives protein, thiamine, zinc and selenium; the belly makes this a rich, fatty roast for a feast, eaten in thin slices.

ingredients.prepNote: wild fennel flowers or fronds are traditional where they grow

instructions: Lay the belly skin side down. Score the meat side in a criss-cross. Mix the salt, sugar, pepper, fennel, garlic and chopped herbs and rub most of it into the meat.
Rub the tenderloin with the rest of the mixture and the oil, lay it along one long edge with the bay leaves and roll the belly tightly round it. Tie with string every 2 to 3 cm.
Prick the skin all over with the tip of a knife, then leave the roll uncovered in the fridge 6 hours or overnight so the skin dries.
Roast on a rack over a tray with the wine and a little water at 250 °F (120 °C) until the center reads 145 °F (62 °C), about 3 to 4 hours. Keep a little liquid in the tray.
Keep roasting until the center reaches 172 to 180 °F (78 to 82 °C), then rest the roll 30 minutes.
Raise the oven to 430 °F (220 °C) and roast 20 to 30 minutes until the skin puffs and crackles. Rest 10 minutes and cut into thin slices, warm or cold, often in a crusty roll.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork tenderloin and belly.
Pork is one of the richest sources.

citations.source: Giallo Zafferano blog (Il caldo sapore del sud), Porchetta fatta in casa
Giallo Zafferano blog (Esplosione di gusto), Porchetta fatta in casa con procedimento completo

recipes.curationNote: Il caldo sapore del sud gives the quantities (2.5 kg belly, 600 g tenderloin, bay, rosemary, sage, parsley, garlic, pepper, 25 g salt, 25 g sugar, 6 h marinade, 120 °C to 62 °C core then on to 78 to 82 °C, rest, 220 °C 30 minutes); Esplosione di gusto adds fennel seed and white wine in the tray. Pork belly with skin is not in the database.
