recipes.name: Polpette al Sugo
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, savoury meatballs of beef and sausage with milk-soaked bread, Parmigiano and parsley, browned and then simmered slowly in tomato sauce until tender.
recipes.healthBenefit: The beef and egg give protein, iron, zinc and vitamin B12, and the tomato sauce adds lycopene and potassium.

ingredients.name: fresh Italian pork sausage (salsiccia), skin removed

ingredients.baseName: Pain, baguette ou boule, de campagne
Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.prepNote: for browning

instructions: Soak the bread in the milk for 10 minutes, then squeeze it well and crumble it.
Mix the beef, sausage meat, bread, Parmigiano, egg, parsley, garlic, nutmeg, salt and pepper by hand until it holds together. Do not overwork it.
With damp hands roll balls about the size of a walnut. Chill them 20 to 30 minutes so they firm up.
Brown the meatballs in the oil in a wide pan over medium heat, turning gently, 5 to 6 minutes.
Pour in the tomato sauce, cover and simmer gently for 30 to 40 minutes, turning them once, until cooked through and the sauce has thickened. Add the basil at the end.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the beef, sausage and egg.

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (250 g beef, 150 g sausage, breadcrumbs, Parmigiano, egg, parsley, garlic, nutmeg, fried, then a sauce of passata) and Misya (500 g beef, bread soaked in milk, pecorino, 2 eggs, 1 litre passata, chilled 30 minutes, 40 minutes in the sauce). Combined: beef and sausage from Dissapore, milk-soaked bread and the long simmer from Misya. The sauce points at sugo di pomodoro.

recipes.name: Abbacchio alla Romana
recipes.flavorProfile: Young milk-fed lamb roasted in pieces with garlic, rosemary and sage, basted with white wine and vinegar, and finished with a sharp paste of anchovy, garlic and vinegar that makes it savoury and bright.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lamb gives protein, iron, zinc and vitamin B12; the anchovy adds a little omega-3 and a good deal of salt.

ingredients.prepNote: weight given is the meat; about 1.5 kg of milk lamb with bone in all

ingredients.cutPrep: 3 to 4 salted anchovies, rinsed and boned
3 cloves, 2 crushed and 1 for the paste

instructions: Heat the oven to 350 °F (180 °C). Season the lamb with salt and pepper and toss it in a roasting pan with the oil, crushed garlic, rosemary, sage and bay.
Roast 20 minutes, then pour over the wine and half the vinegar.
Roast 40 to 50 minutes more, turning and basting the pieces every 15 minutes, until the meat is browned and comes easily from the bone.
Meanwhile pound the anchovies with the last garlic clove and a few rosemary needles, and loosen the paste with the rest of the vinegar.
Spoon the paste over the lamb, stir it through the juices and return to the oven 5 minutes. Serve hot with roast potatoes.

citations.source: Giallo Zafferano blog (Il ricettario timo e lavanda), Abbacchio alla romana

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (1.5 kg milk lamb, 3 anchovies, garlic, rosemary, sage, bay, white wine and vinegar, 180 °C about 1 h basting, anchovy paste at the end) and Il ricettario timo e lavanda (1 kg lamb, 4 anchovies, wine, half a glass of vinegar, covered pan 40 minutes) agree on the anchovy and vinegar finish. Oven method kept. Meat weight entered without bone, split between shoulder and leg.

recipes.name: Pollo al Mattone
recipes.flavorProfile: A whole chicken opened flat, marinated in lemon, olive oil, sage, rosemary and garlic and cooked pressed under a brick, so the skin turns crisp and golden all over and the meat stays juicy.
recipes.healthBenefit: The chicken gives protein, niacin, vitamin B6 and selenium, and the herbs and lemon bring flavour with little added salt.

ingredients.cutPrep: 1 chicken of about 2.2 kg, backbone removed and pressed flat
ingredients.prepNote: weight given is the meat with skin, without bone

instructions: Mix the oil, lemon zest and juice, sage, rosemary, garlic, salt, oregano, chili and pepper. Rub it all over the flattened chicken and under the skin, and leave it 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 480 °F (250 °C) with two heavy trays or a cast iron pan inside.
Lay the chicken skin side down, set a hot tray on top and weigh it down with a brick wrapped in foil or a heavy pot.
Cook 20 to 25 minutes, until the skin is deep gold. Turn the chicken, put the weight back and cook 15 to 20 minutes more, until the thigh juices run clear (165 °F, 74 °C).
Rest 10 minutes, then cut into pieces and spoon the pan juices over.

citations.source: Audrey Le Goff, Pollo al mattone (Tuscan brick roast chicken)

recipes.curationNote: Audrey Le Goff (2.2 kg spatchcocked chicken, 120 ml oil, lemon, 12 sage leaves, rosemary, garlic, oregano, chili, 2 h marinade, 250 °C under hot trays and a brick, 25 plus 20 minutes, rest 10) followed; Dissapore confirms the weight and about 1 hour of cooking with dried herbs. Chicken entered without bone.

recipes.name: Coda alla Vaccinara
recipes.flavorProfile: Oxtail stewed for hours in tomato and wine until it slips off the bone, finished with a pile of celery, a little bittersweet cocoa, raisins and pine nuts for a sauce that is deep, sticky and sweet-sour.
recipes.healthBenefit: Oxtail gives protein, zinc and collagen, celery and tomato add potassium and vitamin K, and the lard and long cooking make it a rich dish.

ingredients.name: oxtail, cut through the joints
ingredients.cutPrep: soaked in cold water 1 hour, dried

ingredients.prepNote: or guanciale, as some Roman cooks prefer

instructions: Melt the lard with the oil in a heavy casserole and brown the oxtail pieces well on all sides, 10 to 15 minutes.
Add the onion, carrot, garlic, chili and cloves and cook until soft, about 10 minutes. Pour in the wine and let it bubble off.
Add the tomatoes and a cup of hot water, season with salt and pepper, cover and simmer very gently for 3 to 4 hours, until the meat comes away from the bone. Add hot water if it gets dry.
Blanch the celery in salted water 5 minutes, drain, and add it to the pot for the last 20 to 30 minutes.
Stir a ladle of sauce into the cocoa, then stir it back in with the raisins and pine nuts. Simmer 10 minutes more and serve; the leftover sauce dresses rigatoni.

citations.source: Scatti di Gusto, Coda alla vaccinara: la ricetta originale

recipes.curationNote: Scatti di Gusto (1.5 kg oxtail, 1.5 kg peeled tomatoes, lard or guanciale, soffritto, 6 celery stalks, wine, cloves, pine nuts, raisins, 2 tbsp cocoa, at least 3 h) followed for the long cook; Dissapore (1 kg oxtail, 50 g lard, cocoa, celery, pine nuts, raisins) agrees on the finish. Oxtail is not in the database.

recipes.name: Salsiccia e Friarielli
recipes.flavorProfile: Fresh pork sausages browned and splashed with wine, then tossed with bitter, garlicky broccoli rabe sautéed in olive oil with chili, a sharp and satisfying Neapolitan pairing.
recipes.healthBenefit: Broccoli rabe is rich in vitamin K, vitamin C, folate and calcium, and the sausage gives protein; the sausage brings salt and fat, so this is a hearty plate.

ingredients.cutPrep: friarielli, tough stems and yellow leaves removed
ingredients.prepNote: about 600 g once cleaned

instructions: Brown the sausages in a tablespoon of oil over medium heat, turning, 8 to 10 minutes. Pour in the wine, let it bubble off, add a splash of water and cook 10 minutes more until done through.
Meanwhile warm the rest of the oil with the garlic and chili in a large pan. Add the friarielli still wet from washing, with a pinch of salt.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender and reduced.
Add the sausages and their juices to the greens and toss together over the heat 3 to 4 minutes. Serve hot with bread.

citations.source: Giallo Zafferano blog (Carmencita81), Salsicce e friarielli

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (4 sausages, 500 g friarielli, 8 tbsp oil, chili, garlic, half a glass of wine, combined 3 to 4 minutes) and Carmencita81 (1.5 kg friarielli for 6, garlic, chili, wine and water, friarielli 15 to 20 minutes). Friarielli entered as broccoli rabe, the same plant. Sausage is not in the database.

recipes.name: Braciole alla Napoletana
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin slices of beef rolled round garlic, parsley, cheese, raisins and pine nuts, browned and simmered for a long time in tomato until tender, with a sweet, savoury filling and a dark sauce that also dresses the pasta.
recipes.healthBenefit: The beef gives protein, iron, zinc and vitamin B12, and the tomato sauce adds lycopene and potassium.

ingredients.cutPrep: grated, or provolone in small pieces

ingredients.prepNote: or olive oil

instructions: Pound the beef slices between baking paper until thin. Pound half the garlic with the parsley and a pinch of salt and pepper into a paste.
Spread the paste over each slice, scatter with the cheese, raisins and pine nuts, roll up tightly and tie with string or pin with toothpicks.

Melt the lard in a heavy pan and brown the rolls on all sides, 5 to 6 minutes. Add the onion and the rest of the garlic, cover and cook gently until the onion is very soft, 8 to 10 minutes, adding a spoon of water if it catches.
Raise the heat, pour in the wine and let it bubble off while turning the rolls.
Add the passata, lower the heat, cover and simmer very gently for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until the meat is tender and the sauce dark and thick, adding water if it reduces too much.
Remove the string, add the basil and serve the braciole with a little sauce; the rest of the sauce traditionally dresses ziti or rigatoni as the first course.

citations.source: Memorie di Angelina, Braciole alla napoletana
Giallo Zafferano blog (Ricette pane e dolci), Braciole napoletane

recipes.curationNote: Memorie di Angelina (8 slices, parsley and garlic paste, cheese, raisins, pine nuts, lard, onion, red wine, 500 g passata, an hour or more) followed; Napolike (raisins soaked in Aglianico, braised in ragù 2 to 3 h) and Ricette pane e dolci (4 slices, Parmigiano, parsley, garlic, 500 g passata, at least 1 h) compared. A self-contained tomato sauce is used rather than the full ragù.

recipes.name: Maiale al Latte
recipes.flavorProfile: Pork loin browned and then cooked slowly in milk with garlic, rosemary and sage, so the meat stays tender and the milk turns into a nutty, golden sauce that is blended smooth.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork loin is lean and gives protein, thiamine and selenium, and the milk adds calcium.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Season the pork with salt and pepper. Brown it all over in the butter and oil in a heavy casserole that just fits it, 8 to 10 minutes.
Add the onion, carrot, garlic and herbs and cook 5 minutes until soft. Pour in the wine and let it bubble off.

Pour in the milk, which should come about halfway up the meat. Bring to a bare simmer, cover partly and cook over low heat for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, turning the meat every 20 minutes, until the center reads 150 to 155 °F (65 to 68 °C).
Lift out the pork and rest it 10 minutes. Remove the herbs and blend the milk and vegetables into a smooth sauce, reducing it a little if thin.
Slice the pork and serve with the warm sauce.

citations.source: Dissapore, Arista di maiale al latte
Giallo Zafferano blog (Il caldo sapore del sud), Lonza di maiale al latte

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (1 kg loin, garlic, onion, carrot, rosemary, bay, sage, 500 ml milk, 180 °C about 1 h, sauce blended) and Il caldo sapore del sud (1 kg loin, 1 litre milk, butter and oil, 150 ml white wine, about 2 h on the stove, core 68 °C). Stove method with 750 ml milk taken between the two.

recipes.name: Trippa alla Romana
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender strips of tripe stewed in a soffritto and tomato sauce scented with cloves, then finished with a snow of Pecorino Romano and fresh mint, soft and savoury with a cool herbal lift.
recipes.healthBenefit: Tripe is a lean source of protein, vitamin B12 and selenium, and the Pecorino adds calcium.

ingredients.name: beef tripe (honeycomb and blanket), cleaned and precooked
mentuccia (lesser calamint) leaves
ingredients.prepNote: spearmint is used where mentuccia cannot be found

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and blanch the tripe 10 to 15 minutes. Drain, rinse and cut into strips about 1 cm wide.
Warm the oil and gently cook the onion, carrot, celery, garlic and chili until soft, 8 to 10 minutes. Remove the garlic.
Add the tripe and let it take colour for about 10 minutes. Pour in the wine and let it bubble off.
Add the passata, cloves and rosemary, season with salt and pepper, cover and simmer 30 to 40 minutes, until the tripe is tender and the sauce thick.
Turn off the heat, stir in a handful of Pecorino and half the mint torn small. Serve with more Pecorino and the rest of the mint on top.

citations.source: Scatti di Gusto, Trippa alla romana: la ricetta originale della Sora Lella

recipes.curationNote: Sora Lella via Scatti di Gusto (1 kg tripe blanched 15 minutes, soffritto, 1 kg passed tomatoes, 2 cloves, half a glass of white wine, 150 g Pecorino, mentuccia at the end, 30 minutes) and Dissapore (500 ml passata, 3 cloves, rosemary, 100 g Pecorino, 12 mint leaves, 40 minutes). Tripe and mentuccia are not in the database.

recipes.name: Scaloppine al Limone
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin floured veal slices seared in butter and oil in a few minutes and bathed in a light, glossy lemon sauce, tender, tangy and buttery.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean veal gives protein, niacin and vitamin B12, and the dish is quick and light for a meat course.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.cutPrep: juiced, plus a few slices to serve

instructions: Pound the veal slices lightly to an even thickness. Dust them with flour and shake off the excess.
Warm the oil and butter with the thyme in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Sear the slices 1 to 2 minutes a side until lightly golden at the edges, then lift them out.
Pour the wine into the hot pan and let it bubble off, then add the lemon juice and scrape up the browned bits.
Return the veal with a pinch of salt and pepper and turn it in the sauce over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, no longer, or it toughens.
Serve at once with the sauce spooned over, chopped parsley and lemon slices.

citations.source: Giallo Zafferano blog (Ricette pane e dolci), Scaloppine di vitello al limone

recipes.curationNote: Ricette pane e dolci (600 g veal, flour, 30 g butter and oil, 50 ml white wine, 1 lemon, 2 to 3 minutes in the sauce) followed; Dissapore (8 slices, oil with thyme, lemon juice, parsley and lemon slices) compared and its thyme kept as optional.

recipes.name: Involtini di Manzo
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin beef slices rolled round prosciutto, carrot and celery, browned and slowly simmered in tomato sauce until tender, savoury and sweet with a sauce rich enough for pasta.
recipes.healthBenefit: The beef gives protein, iron, zinc and vitamin B12, and the vegetables and tomato add vitamin A, potassium and lycopene.

ingredients.cutPrep: half in thin sticks for the rolls, half finely chopped
half in thin sticks for the rolls, half finely chopped

instructions: Pound the beef slices thin and season lightly with salt. Lay a slice of prosciutto on each, then a stick of carrot, a stick of celery and a basil leaf at one end.
Roll each up tightly and pin with a toothpick or tie with string.
Warm the oil in a wide pan and cook the chopped onion, carrot, celery and a garlic clove gently 5 minutes. Add the rolls and brown them well on all sides.
Raise the heat, pour in the wine and let it bubble off, 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the passata and a splash of warm water, season, cover and simmer over low heat for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, turning the rolls now and then and adding water if the sauce gets too thick.
Stir in the parsley a few minutes before the end. Remove the toothpicks and serve the involtini with their sauce, or use the sauce for pasta first.

citations.source: Giallo Zafferano blog (Il chicco di mais), Involtini al sugo ricetta romana
Turismo Roma, Involtini di carne alla romana

recipes.curationNote: Il chicco di mais (800 g beef slices, 150 g prosciutto, carrot and celery sticks inside, 500 g passata, wine, at least 1 hour) and Turismo Roma (8 slices of 60 to 70 g, raw ham, carrot, celery, basil and garlic inside, soffritto, 600 g peeled tomatoes, 50 to 60 minutes, parsley at the end) agree. Prosciutto entered as cured ham.

recipes.name: Carciofi alla Romana
recipes.flavorProfile: Whole Roman artichokes stuffed with garlic, mint and parsley and stewed upside down in olive oil and a little water, so the hearts turn meltingly soft and the leaves soak up the herby oil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Artichokes bring fibre, including inulin that feeds gut bacteria, plus folate, vitamin K and potassium, and the olive oil adds mostly monounsaturated fat.

ingredients.cutPrep: 8 mammole artichokes, trimmed to the pale leaves, stems peeled
ingredients.prepNote: weight given is after trimming

ingredients.name: mentuccia (lesser calamint) leaves
ingredients.prepNote: spearmint is used where mentuccia cannot be found

instructions: Pull off the tough outer leaves until the pale ones show, cut off the hard tips and peel the stems, keeping about 4 cm. Open each artichoke and scoop out any choke. Drop them into water with the lemon juice as you go.
Mix the garlic, mentuccia and parsley with 2 tablespoons of the oil, salt and pepper.
Drain the artichokes, open the leaves gently and press the herb mixture into the center and between the leaves.
Stand them upside down, stems up, close together in a deep narrow pan. Pour over the rest of the oil and the water, about a finger deep.
Cover with a damp sheet of crumpled baking paper and the lid and cook over low heat 20 to 30 minutes, without opening, until a fork slides easily into the heart.
Serve warm or at room temperature with the cooking oil spooned over.

citations.source: Giallo Zafferano blog (Il chicco di mais), Carciofi alla romana

recipes.curationNote: Misya (5 artichokes, parsley, garlic, mint, 2 tbsp oil in the stuffing, upside down with a finger of water, 25 minutes low heat) and Il chicco di mais (8 mammole for 4, mentuccia, 6 tbsp oil, 100 ml water, wet parchment under the lid, 20 to 25 minutes) agree. Mentuccia is not in the database; Misya allows ordinary mint in its place.

recipes.name: Carciofi alla Giudia
recipes.flavorProfile: Whole artichokes fried twice until they open like a bronze flower, the outer leaves crisp and nutty like chips and the heart soft and sweet, with nothing but salt.
recipes.healthBenefit: Artichokes bring fibre, folate and potassium; deep fried, this is a rich dish best eaten in small numbers.

ingredients.cutPrep: 8 large round mammole, only the toughest outer leaves removed, stems trimmed short
ingredients.prepNote: weight given is after trimming

ingredients.name: seed oil for frying (peanut or sunflower)
ingredients.prepNote: the share taken up; fry in about 1 litre

instructions: Remove only the toughest outer leaves, trim the tips by about a third and leave a short stem. Soak in water with the lemon juice for 10 minutes, then pat completely dry.
Tap each artichoke upside down on the board to open the leaves a little, and scoop out the choke.

Heat the oil in a deep pot to 285 to 300 °F (140 to 150 °C). Fry the artichokes two or three at a time for about 10 minutes, turning, until a toothpick slides easily into the base. Drain upside down on paper.
When cool enough to touch, spread the leaves outward like petals and season inside and out with salt and pepper.
Raise the oil to 355 °F (180 °C). Fry them again, flower side down, pressing gently against the bottom of the pan, 2 to 3 minutes until the leaves are deep amber and crisp.
Drain upside down on paper and serve at once.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (peanut oil, first fry 140 to 150 °C, salt between, second fry 180 °C 2 to 3 minutes upside down, no lemon soak) and Misya (4 mammole, lemon soak 10 minutes, first fry about 10 minutes, salt and pepper, second fry until deep amber) agree on the double fry. Dissapore temperatures with the Misya times and soak. Frying oil entered as the share taken up.

recipes.name: Parmigiana di Melanzane
recipes.flavorProfile: Layers of fried eggplant, tomato sauce, melting mozzarella, Parmigiano and basil baked until bubbling and golden, soft, rich and deeply savoury.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggplant and tomato bring fibre, potassium and lycopene and the cheeses bring protein and calcium; with the fried eggplant it is a rich dish.

ingredients.cutPrep: long dark eggplants, sliced lengthwise 3 to 5 mm thick

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.name: seed oil for frying (peanut or sunflower)
ingredients.prepNote: the share taken up; fry in about 1 litre

instructions: Layer the eggplant slices in a colander with salt and leave them 30 minutes to give up their water. Rinse, squeeze gently and pat dry.
Dust the slices lightly with flour and fry them in hot oil, 340 to 355 °F (170 to 180 °C), a few at a time, 2 to 3 minutes a side until golden. Drain on paper.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (180 °C). Spread a little tomato sauce in a baking dish about 20 by 30 cm.
Lay down a layer of eggplant, then sauce, mozzarella, a generous scatter of Parmigiano and a few basil leaves. Repeat until everything is used, finishing with sauce and plenty of Parmigiano.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, then 5 minutes under a hot grill until the top is browned.
Let it rest at least 20 to 30 minutes before cutting; it is often eaten warm or at room temperature.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (1 kg eggplant salted 30 minutes, floured and fried, 500 ml passata cooked with garlic and oil, 300 g mozzarella, 100 g Parmigiano, basil, 180 °C 30 minutes then grill 5) followed; Misya (same weights, 50 g Parmigiano, an egg poured over the fried slices) compared and the egg left out. The sauce points at sugo di pomodoro.

recipes.name: Peperonata
recipes.flavorProfile: Red and yellow peppers stewed slowly with onion and tomato until soft and sweet, with a light sweet-sour edge from a pinch of sugar and a splash of vinegar.
recipes.healthBenefit: Peppers are among the richest vegetables in vitamin C and bring vitamin A carotenoids, and the tomato adds lycopene.
instructions: Remove the stems, seeds and white ribs from the peppers and cut them into pieces about 2 cm.
Warm the oil in a wide pan and cook the onion and garlic gently until soft, 5 to 8 minutes.
Add the peppers and cook over medium heat, stirring now and then, about 15 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, add the tomatoes, cover and cook 15 minutes more, until the peppers are soft but still hold their shape.
Stir in the sugar, then the vinegar, and let it bubble over high heat for a minute until its sharpness fades. Remove the garlic.
Take off the heat, tear in the basil and rest 10 to 15 minutes before serving, warm or at room temperature.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the red and yellow peppers.

recipes.curationNote: Misya gives the amounts and times (2 peppers, spring onion, garlic, 200 g tomatoes, 15 plus 15 minutes) for 4; Dissapore adds the guidance kept here: mostly red and yellow peppers in 2 cm chunks, a teaspoon of sugar per two peppers, a splash of vinegar at the end, rest 10 to 15 minutes. Pepper quantity raised to four for four people as a side.

recipes.name: Fagioli all'Uccelletto
recipes.flavorProfile: Creamy white beans warmed in olive oil with garlic and sage and simmered briefly with a little tomato, plain, soft and fragrant.
recipes.healthBenefit: White beans bring plant protein, fibre, folate, iron and potassium, and with olive oil this is a filling, nourishing side.

ingredients.cutPrep: 3 cloves, 1 for the cooking water and 2 crushed for the pan

instructions: Soak the beans overnight in plenty of cold water. Drain and rinse.

Cover them with fresh water in a pot with one garlic clove and the bay leaf. Simmer very gently, skimming now and then, for 50 to 70 minutes until tender. Salt near the end. Drain, keeping a cup of the cooking water, and discard the garlic and bay.
Warm the oil in a wide pan, ideally earthenware, with the crushed garlic and the sage until the sage starts to crisp.
Add the beans and stir to coat, then add the passata, a ladle of the cooking water, salt and pepper.
Simmer gently, covered, 15 to 20 minutes until the sauce has thickened and clings to the beans. Serve with a thread of raw oil, often beside grilled sausages.

citations.source: Visit Tuscany, La ricetta dei fagioli all'uccelletto

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (300 g dried cannellini soaked, boiled with garlic and bay at least 50 minutes, then garlic in oil and 200 ml passata) followed; Visit Tuscany (garlic and sage in oil until the sage crisps, cooking water, tomato, about 20 minutes, earthenware, sausages beside) adds the sage that gives the dish its name. Sausages left out to keep it a side.

recipes.name: Cicoria Ripassata
recipes.flavorProfile: Bitter chicory greens boiled tender, squeezed and then tossed hard in a pan with plenty of olive oil, garlic and chili, so they are silky, bitter and gently hot.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicory greens are rich in vitamin K, vitamin A carotenoids, folate and fibre, and their bitterness comes from plant compounds the greens are known for.
instructions: Soak the chicory in a sink of cold water to loosen the soil, cut off the tough base of the leaves and rinse each leaf well.
Boil in salted water 10 to 15 minutes until tender. Drain, let it cool a little and squeeze out as much water as you can. Chop it roughly.
Warm the oil in a wide pan with the garlic and chili until they sizzle, without letting the garlic brown.
Add the chicory and cook over high heat about 5 minutes, stirring and dragging it round the pan so it takes up the oil. Taste for salt and serve hot or warm.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (1.5 kg chicory, garlic, fresh chili, 5 tbsp oil, boiled 10 minutes, squeezed, 5 minutes on high heat) and Turismo Roma (boiled in salted water, squeezed, plenty of oil, garlic and chili, stirred so it soaks up the flavours, "strascinata") agree. Dissapore boils in only 200 ml of water under a lid; a full pot of salted water is used here as Turismo Roma describes.

recipes.name: Patate al Forno
recipes.flavorProfile: Potato chunks roasted in olive oil with rosemary and garlic until the edges are crisp and golden and the middles soft and fluffy.
recipes.healthBenefit: Potatoes bring potassium, vitamin C and vitamin B6, and roasting in olive oil keeps the fat mostly monounsaturated.

ingredients.cutPrep: yellow-fleshed, peeled and cut in even 3 cm chunks

instructions: Soak the potato chunks in cold salted water 10 to 30 minutes to draw off some starch, then drain and dry well in a cloth.
Heat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Put the oil, garlic, rosemary and chili in a roasting dish large enough to hold the potatoes in one layer.
Add the potatoes, season with pepper and toss so every piece is coated.
Roast 30 minutes, turning them halfway, then lower to 350 °F (180 °C) and roast 10 to 15 minutes more until golden all over. A final 5 minutes under the grill makes them crisper.
Salt and serve hot.
recipes.curationNote: Misya (1.2 kg yellow potatoes, oil, garlic, rosemary, chili, 10 minute salted soak, 180 °C 30 minutes then 5 under the grill) and Dissapore (30 to 60 minute soak, unpeeled garlic, 200 °C 30 minutes then 180 °C about 10, single layer). Dissapore oven sequence kept; its parboil step left out as Misya does without it.

recipes.name: Zucchine alla Scapece
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin rounds of zucchini fried golden and then left to marinate in vinegar with raw garlic and fresh mint, so they turn soft, tangy and cool.
recipes.healthBenefit: Zucchini bring vitamin C, potassium and some fibre; fried, this is a richer side best served in small amounts.

ingredients.cutPrep: 4 to 6 firm zucchini, in rounds 3 to 5 mm thick

ingredients.name: seed oil for frying (peanut or sunflower)
ingredients.prepNote: the share taken up; fry in about 500 ml

ingredients.cutPrep: 2 cloves, 1 to flavour the oil and 1 thinly sliced

instructions: Slice the zucchini into rounds and spread them on a cotton cloth to dry for 1 to 2 hours, in the sun if you can. Without sun, sprinkle with coarse salt and leave until they give up their water, then pat dry.
Heat the oil in a deep pan with one garlic clove until it sizzles, then remove it.
Fry the zucchini in batches at about 340 to 355 °F (170 to 180 °C), 3 to 5 minutes, until golden brown. Drain well on paper.
In a glass or ceramic dish, layer the zucchini with the sliced garlic, torn mint and a pinch of salt, sprinkling vinegar over each layer. Finish with a thread of raw olive oil.
Cover and leave at least 2 hours, better 12 to 24 in the fridge, before serving at room temperature.

citations.source: Dissapore, La ricetta perfetta: zucchine alla scapece

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (6 Neapolitan zucchini in 3 to 5 mm rounds dried in the sun 1 to 2 hours, fried, layered with garlic, mint, salt and a glass of white vinegar, rested 12 to 24 hours) and Napolike (3 to 4 zucchini, seed oil, garlic, 4 to 5 mint leaves, vinegar and raw oil to finish). Frying oil entered as the share taken up.

recipes.name: Funghi Trifolati
recipes.region: Throughout Italy (Piedmont and Tuscany for wild mushrooms)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sliced mushrooms cooked in their juices and then sautéed in olive oil with garlic and finished with plenty of parsley, earthy, garlicky and tender.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mushrooms bring B vitamins including riboflavin and niacin, potassium and selenium, with very few calories.

ingredients.prepNote: or other wild mushrooms such as chanterelles

instructions: Trim the earthy ends of the stems and wipe the mushrooms clean with a damp cloth. Slice the larger ones and leave small ones whole.
Put the cultivated mushrooms in a dry pan, cover and cook about 10 minutes until they release their water. Drain them and set aside.
Warm the oil with the garlic and the chili, if using, until the garlic is golden, then remove the garlic.
Add the porcini and the cultivated mushrooms and sauté over high heat 2 to 3 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Cover and cook 5 to 10 minutes more until tender. Stir in plenty of chopped parsley off the heat and serve hot or at room temperature.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (300 g porcini, 200 g honey mushrooms, 200 g chanterelles, garlic browned in 4 tbsp oil, quick sauté, 5 minutes covered, parsley) and Misya (500 g champignon cooked dry first to release water, then garlic and optional chili, 10 minutes covered, plenty of parsley). Combined: porcini from Dissapore with cultivated mushrooms as Misya uses, each handled as its source says.

recipes.name: Verdure Grigliate
recipes.flavorProfile: Slices of eggplant, zucchini, pepper, onion and cherry tomatoes charred on a hot grill and dressed with olive oil, garlic and rosemary, smoky, sweet and soft.
recipes.healthBenefit: A mix of vegetables that brings fibre, vitamin C, potassium and carotenoids, with olive oil for mostly monounsaturated fat.

ingredients.cutPrep: 1 pepper, in strips at least 4 cm wide

instructions: Mix 2 tablespoons of the oil with salt, pepper and the rosemary needles, and brush it over the cut vegetables.

Heat a ridged grill pan or barbecue until very hot. Grill the vegetables a few at a time so each slice lies flat on the surface: eggplant and zucchini 2 to 3 minutes a side, onion 3 to 4, pepper strips 4 to 5, tomatoes last as they give off water.
Lay everything on a serving plate.
Dress with the rest of the oil, the vinegar if using, the sliced garlic and a few more rosemary needles.
Leave them about an hour at room temperature before serving so the flavours settle.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the eggplant and other vegetables.

citations.source: Scatti di Gusto, Verdure grigliate: come cucinare melanzane, peperoni, zucchine, pomodori

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore gives the quantities (1 zucchini, 1 yellow pepper, 1 eggplant, 8 cherry tomatoes, white and Tropea onion, 30 ml oil with salt, pepper and rosemary, garlic slices to finish, rest about an hour); Scatti di Gusto adds the dressing of oil, a little wine vinegar and garlic for zucchini and eggplant. Grill times added from usual practice since neither gives them.

recipes.name: Insalata di Finocchi e Arance
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, aniseed-sweet fennel with juicy orange slices and salty black olives under a glug of olive oil, bright, cool and refreshing.
recipes.healthBenefit: Oranges and fennel bring vitamin C, potassium and fibre, and the olives and walnuts add mostly unsaturated fats.

ingredients.cutPrep: 3 to 4 round bulbs, trimmed and thinly sliced
Tarocco or blood oranges, peeled to the flesh and sliced or in pieces

instructions: Trim the fennel, keep a few fronds, and slice the bulbs thinly. Rinse in cold water and dry.
Grate a little orange zest and set it aside. Peel the oranges with a knife, taking off all the white pith, and slice them or cut them into pieces, keeping the juice.
Put the fennel, oranges and their juice, and the olives in a bowl. Add the walnuts if using.
Dress with oil, salt and a pinch of pepper and toss gently.
Scatter the zest and fennel fronds over and serve, or leave 20 to 30 minutes for the flavours to meet.

citations.source: Giallo Zafferano blog (Mela cannella e fantasia), Finocchi, arance e olive alla siciliana
GreenMe, Insalata di finocchi e arance

recipes.curationNote: Mela cannella e fantasia (1 fennel, 2 oranges, 15 black olives for 2, oil, salt, pepper, zest, walnuts optional) and GreenMe (4 fennel, 2 Tarocco oranges, 100 g olives, 100 g walnuts for 4). Quantities set between the two; walnuts kept optional.

components.note: about 240 ml, hot

recipes.name: Piselli al Prosciutto
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet green peas cooked quickly with soft onion and strips of prosciutto in a little broth, tender, sweet and lightly salty.
recipes.healthBenefit: Peas bring plant protein, fibre, vitamin C, vitamin K and folate, and the prosciutto adds flavour and some salt.

ingredients.cutPrep: or the same weight of fresh shelled peas
prosciutto crudo, 3 to 4 slices, in thin strips

instructions: Warm the oil in a pan and cook the onion gently until soft and translucent, 5 to 6 minutes.
Add the prosciutto strips and stir 1 to 2 minutes until they lose their raw look.
Add the peas straight from the freezer and stir over high heat 2 minutes.
Pour in the hot broth, lower the heat and cook 5 to 8 minutes, or 15 to 20 minutes for fresh peas, until tender and most of the liquid has gone.
Taste before adding salt, since the prosciutto brings plenty, grind over some pepper and serve hot, warm or cold.

citations.source: Memorie di Angelina, Piselli alla romana
Giallo Zafferano blog (Allacciate il grembiule), Piselli e prosciutto

recipes.curationNote: Memorie di Angelina (450 g peas, half an onion, 2 to 3 slices of prosciutto in strips, about 5 minutes for frozen and 15 to 20 for fresh) for the Roman crudo version; Allacciate il grembiule (600 g frozen peas, onion, a glass of vegetable broth, 3 tbsp oil, about 10 minutes, with cooked ham) for the broth and amounts. Prosciutto crudo kept, as in Rome. Broth points at brodo vegetale.

recipes.name: Tiramisù
recipes.flavorProfile: Ladyfingers soaked in strong coffee layered with a light, airy cream of mascarpone, egg and sugar and finished with bitter cocoa, soft, creamy and gently bitter.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich dessert of mascarpone, eggs and sugar; the eggs bring protein, and it is best kept to a small square.
instructions: Make the coffee and let it cool completely.
Separate the eggs. Whip the whites with a pinch of salt to stiff peaks.
Whisk the yolks with the sugar until pale, thick and frothy, then fold in the mascarpone a spoonful at a time, lifting from the bottom so the cream stays light.
Fold in the whipped whites in two or three goes.

Spread a thin layer of cream in a dish about 20 by 30 cm. Dip the ladyfingers in the coffee one at a time for a second or two on each side, so they soften without falling apart, and lay them close together.
Cover with cream, then another layer of soaked ladyfingers, and finish with cream.
Dust generously with cocoa and chill at least 2 hours, better 4 to 6 or overnight, before cutting.

nutritionHighlights.note: Mascarpone is a very rich cheese.

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (750 g mascarpone, 5 eggs separated, whites whipped, 120 g sugar, 250 g savoiardi, 6 cups of moka coffee, cocoa, 2 hours chilling) followed as the classic egg and mascarpone cream. Misya (yolks only, mascarpone lightened with whipped cream, milk in the coffee, chocolate shavings, about 3 hours) compared; its cream and chocolate left out. The eggs are not cooked, so use the freshest eggs you can, or pasteurised eggs for anyone pregnant, very young, elderly or with a weakened immune system.

recipes.name: Panna Cotta
recipes.flavorProfile: Cream and milk scented with vanilla, set with just enough gelatine to wobble, smooth and milky, served with a warm sauce of strawberries cooked with sugar and lemon.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich cream dessert; the strawberries bring vitamin C, and it is best kept to a small mould.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Soak the gelatine sheets in cold water for 10 minutes, then squeeze them out.
Warm the milk, take it off the heat and stir in the gelatine until it dissolves.
In another pan bring the cream, 100 g of sugar and the vanilla just to the boil. Take it off the heat, add the milk and stir well with a whisk.
Rinse four moulds or cups with cold water, shake them out without drying and pour in the cream.
Chill at least 4 hours, better 6, until set.
For the sauce, cook the strawberries with the tablespoon of sugar and the lemon juice over low heat for about 10 minutes.
Dip each mould briefly in hot water, turn out onto plates and spoon the strawberries over.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (500 ml cream, 100 ml milk, 100 g sugar, vanilla, 10 g gelatine, 4 hours, strawberry sauce cooked 10 minutes with lemon and sugar) followed; Misya (500 ml cream, 150 ml milk, 125 g sugar, 8 g fish gelatine, at least 6 hours, caramel) compared. Strawberry sauce kept from Dissapore.

recipes.name: Cannoli Siciliani
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, blistered fried shells scented with Marsala and filled at the last minute with sweet sheep's milk ricotta, chocolate chips and a touch of cinnamon, crunchy outside and cool and creamy within.
recipes.healthBenefit: Ricotta brings protein and calcium; with a fried shell and sugar, one cannolo is a treat rather than a snack.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.name: seed oil for frying (peanut or sunflower)
ingredients.prepNote: the share taken up; fry in about 1 litre

ingredients.cutPrep: sheep's milk, drained in a sieve for several hours

ingredients.name: icing sugar (powdered sugar)
ingredients.prepNote: sifted into the ricotta

ingredients.name: candied cherries or candied orange peel
icing sugar (powdered sugar)
ingredients.prepNote: for dusting

instructions: Drain the ricotta in a fine sieve in the fridge for several hours, or overnight, so it loses its whey.
Mix the flour, sugar, melted butter, egg, Marsala and salt into a firm dough, adding a few drops of water only if needed. Knead until smooth, wrap and rest at least 30 minutes.
Roll the dough very thin, by hand or through a pasta machine down to a thin setting, and cut discs about 10 cm across.
Wrap each disc around a metal cannoli tube, dab the overlap with a little egg white or water and press to seal.
Heat the oil to 340 °F (170 °C) and fry two or three at a time, 1 to 2 minutes, turning, until blistered and golden. Drain on paper, and when cool slide out the tubes.
Press the ricotta through a sieve, then beat in the icing sugar and cinnamon and stir in the chocolate.
Fill the shells with a piping bag or spoon only shortly before serving, press a piece of candied fruit into each end and dust with icing sugar.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (250 g flour, 1 egg, 50 g sugar, 40 g butter, 50 ml Marsala, 1 kg sheep ricotta drained, cinnamon, chocolate chips, candied fruit, peanut oil at 170 °C, 15 cannoli) followed; Misya (adds 5 g cocoa to the shell, 750 g ricotta, 200 g icing sugar, 150 g chocolate chips) gives the filling amounts. Marsala entered as dessert wine.

recipes.name: Zabaione
recipes.flavorProfile: Egg yolks, sugar and Marsala whisked over barely simmering water into a warm, thick, golden foam, sweet and winey.
recipes.healthBenefit: Egg yolks bring protein, vitamin A, vitamin D and choline; it is sweet and carries a little alcohol, so it suits a small cup.
instructions: In a round metal bowl or small pan, whisk the yolks with the sugar until pale and frothy, by hand or with an electric whisk.
Set the bowl over a pan of water that is barely simmering, without the bowl touching the water.
Add the Marsala and keep whisking constantly for about 10 minutes, until the cream is thick, fluffy and holds a trail. Do not let the water boil or the eggs will curdle.
Serve at once, warm, alone or with dry biscuits.
recipes.curationNote: Misya (4 yolks, 4 tbsp sugar, 4 tbsp Marsala, whisked over barely simmering water about 10 minutes) and Dissapore (3 yolks, 75 g sugar, 40 g Marsala, about 10 minutes) agree. Misya amounts kept. The alcohol does not fully cook off at this gentle heat. Marsala entered as dessert wine.

recipes.name: Cantucci
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp twice-baked almond biscuits, golden and crunchy with whole almonds and a hint of lemon, made for dipping in vin santo.
recipes.healthBenefit: Almonds bring vitamin E, magnesium and fibre; these are still sweet biscuits, best enjoyed one or two at a time.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium-low heat for about 5 minutes, stirring, and let them cool.
Beat the eggs with the sugar, lemon zest, vanilla and salt.
Add the flour mixed with the baking powder and work it in, then the almonds, until the dough is even and holds together.
Shape it into two logs about 3 fingers wide and lay them well apart on a lined tray, since they spread.
Bake at 350 °F (180 °C) for 20 to 25 minutes, until lightly golden.
While still warm, cut the logs on the diagonal into slices about 1 cm thick.
Lay the slices cut side up and bake again at 210 to 350 °F (100 to 180 °C) for 10 to 15 minutes, turning halfway, until dry. Cool and keep in a tin.
recipes.curationNote: Misya (250 g flour, 200 g sugar, 125 g almonds with skin, 2 eggs, baking powder, vanilla, lemon zest, 180 °C 25 minutes then 100 °C 15 minutes) and Dissapore (250 g flour, 150 g sugar, 130 g toasted almonds, 2 eggs, lemon zest, 180 °C 20 minutes then about 10 more turned halfway). Sugar set between the two; the second bake given as either source does it.

recipes.name: Torta Caprese
recipes.flavorProfile: A dense, flourless chocolate and almond cake with a thin crisp crust and a moist, fudgy middle, dusted with icing sugar.
recipes.healthBenefit: Almonds bring vitamin E, magnesium and fibre and dark chocolate brings some iron and magnesium; with this much butter and sugar it is a rich cake. Made without wheat flour.

ingredients.cutPrep: in pieces, plus a little for the tin

ingredients.name: icing sugar (powdered sugar)
ingredients.prepNote: for dusting

instructions: Heat the oven to 340 °F (170 °C) and line a 26 cm springform tin with baking paper.
Melt the chocolate in a bowl over simmering water, then stir in the butter until it melts.
Off the heat, stir in the yolks, the ground almonds and the sugar to a smooth batter.
Whip the whites to stiff peaks and fold them in with a spatula, lifting from the bottom.
Pour into the tin and bake 35 to 40 minutes, until the top is set and crisp but the middle is still moist.
Cool in the tin, turn out and dust with icing sugar.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the almonds and dark chocolate.

recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (250 g each of almond flour, butter, dark chocolate and sugar, 6 eggs separated, 26 cm tin, 170 °C 35 minutes, elsewhere on the page 180 °C 35 to 40) followed; Misya (20 cm tin, 140 g chocolate, 100 g butter, 130 g sugar, 150 g almonds, 3 eggs, a teaspoon of baking powder, 180 °C 35 minutes) compared. The baking powder is left out, keeping the cake without leavening as Dissapore makes it.

components.note: about 650 g of the pastry, for the base and lattice

recipes.name: Crostata di Marmellata
recipes.flavorProfile: A buttery, lemon-scented shortcrust tart filled with jam under a lattice of pastry, crumbly and fruity.
recipes.healthBenefit: A simple home tart of pastry and fruit jam; sweet, so best as a slice with coffee or at breakfast now and then.

ingredients.name: fruit jam (apricot, peach or cherry)
ingredients.prepNote: a thick jam holds best

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Make the pastry and chill it at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 340 to 350 °F (170 to 180 °C). Butter and flour a 24 to 26 cm tart tin.
Roll two thirds of the pastry 3 to 4 mm thick on a floured surface, lift it into the tin, trim the edge and prick the base with a fork.
Spread the jam evenly over the base.
Roll out the rest of the pastry, cut strips with a pastry wheel and lay them diagonally across the jam in two directions to make diamonds. Press the ends to the rim.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes until the pastry is golden.
Let it cool completely before slicing so the jam sets.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the butter in the pastry.

recipes.curationNote: Misya (300 g flour frolla, 400 g jam, 26 cm tin, lattice, 180 °C 40 minutes) and Dissapore (250 g flour, 150 g butter frolla, a jar of jam, lattice, 170 °C 35 minutes). The pastry points at pasta frolla; 6 of its 10 servings is close to both pastry amounts.

recipes.name: Affogato al Caffè
recipes.flavorProfile: A scoop of cold vanilla gelato drowned in a shot of hot espresso, so it melts into a sweet, bitter, creamy coffee.
recipes.healthBenefit: A small dessert of gelato and coffee; the espresso brings caffeine, so it is one to have earlier in the day for anyone sensitive to it.

ingredients.name: vanilla or fior di latte gelato
ingredients.prepNote: fior di latte gelato is often made without egg

instructions: Put a scoop of gelato in each of four small glasses or cups and keep them in the freezer while you make the coffee.
Make the espresso, or moka coffee.
Pour the hot coffee straight over the gelato and serve at once, with a spoon.
A splash of amaretto or grappa in each cup, or a spoon of whipped cream, are common additions.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (4 scoops of vanilla gelato, 4 cups of moka coffee, optional grappa or amaretto or cream) and Misya (200 g fior di latte or vanilla gelato for 2, 2 unsweetened espressos, whipped cream and chocolate shavings). The plain version kept. Gelato is not in the database; entered as dairy and egg.

components.note: about 550 g of the pastry, for one 24 cm pastiera

recipes.name: Pastiera Napoletana
recipes.flavorProfile: The Neapolitan Easter tart: a shortcrust shell and lattice around a filling of ricotta, wheat berries cooked in milk, candied peel and orange blossom water, soft, fragrant and lightly spiced.
recipes.healthBenefit: Ricotta and eggs bring protein and calcium and the wheat brings some fibre; it is a sweet, rich tart for a holiday slice.

ingredients.name: cooked wheat berries (grano cotto)
ingredients.prepNote: sold ready cooked in jars in Italy; or soak and boil soft wheat berries

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.name: icing sugar (powdered sugar)
ingredients.prepNote: for dusting

instructions: Simmer the cooked wheat with the milk, butter and lemon peel over low heat, stirring now and then, until creamy and the milk is absorbed, about 20 to 30 minutes. Cool completely and remove the peel.
Press the ricotta through a sieve and beat it with the sugar. Beat in the eggs and yolk one at a time, then the cooled wheat, candied peel, orange blossom water, cinnamon and vanilla.
Heat the oven to 340 to 350 °F (170 to 180 °C). Roll about two thirds of the pastry 3 to 4 mm thick and line a lightly greased 24 cm tin, about 5 cm deep.
Pour in the filling up to half a centimetre below the rim, since it rises in the oven.
Cut seven strips about 2 cm wide from the rest of the pastry and lay them in a diamond lattice, four one way and three the other.
Bake on the low rack 60 to 90 minutes, until the top is an even amber brown.
Cool in the switched-off oven with the door ajar, then completely. It is best made a day or two ahead and kept in the fridge; dust with icing sugar to serve.
recipes.curationNote: Dissapore (butter frolla from 500 g flour for two 24 cm pies; filling 700 g ricotta, 500 g sugar, 500 g cooked wheat, 5 eggs and 2 yolks, 200 ml milk, candied orange and citron, orange blossom water, cinnamon; 170 °C 60 to 90 minutes) halved for one pie; Misya (lard frolla, 350 g wheat cooked with milk, butter and lemon about 30 minutes, 300 g ricotta, 300 g sugar, 3 eggs, 180 °C about 1 hour) compared. Butter frolla points at pasta frolla, whose amounts match Dissapore's. Grano cotto is not in the database.

components.note: about 350 g of the cream

recipes.name: Zeppole di San Giuseppe
recipes.flavorProfile: Rings of choux pastry fried until puffed and golden, filled with a swirl of vanilla pastry cream and topped with a sour cherry in syrup, crisp, soft and creamy.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggs and milk bring protein; fried and filled with cream, these are a feast day pastry.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.name: seed oil for frying (peanut or sunflower)
ingredients.prepNote: the share taken up; fry in about 1 litre

ingredients.cutPrep: amarene in syrup, plus a little syrup

ingredients.name: icing sugar (powdered sugar)
ingredients.prepNote: for dusting

instructions: Make the pastry cream ahead and chill it covered with film touching the surface.
Bring the water, butter and salt to the boil. Tip in all the flour at once and stir hard until the dough is smooth and comes away from the pan, 1 to 2 minutes more.
Spread the dough out to cool, then beat in the eggs and yolk a little at a time until glossy, soft and just holding its shape.
Pipe rings about 7 cm across, two turns high, through a large star nozzle onto squares of baking paper.

instructions: Bring the water, sugar and lemon zest to the boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then let the syrup cool completely.
Stir the strained lemon juice into the cold syrup.
Pour into a wide metal or plastic tray and freeze for 30 minutes.

Break up the ice crystals with a fork or whisk and return it to the freezer. Repeat every 30 minutes, about 5 to 8 times, over 3 to 4 hours, until it is a mass of fine crystals. An ice cream machine churning about 25 minutes does the same job.

instructions: For the caramel, stir the 150 g of sugar with the water in a small pan, then boil without stirring for a few minutes until amber. Pour it into a loaf mould about 25 by 11 cm and tilt to coat the base.
Mix the eggs, yolk and sugar well without whisking in air. Stir in the cocoa, salt, crushed amaretti and rum, then pour in the milk slowly, stirring.
Pour the mixture over the caramel and set the mould in a deep tray. Pour very hot water into the tray to halfway up the mould.

instructions: Knead the flour, water and salt into a smooth, firm dough, cover and rest 30 minutes.

Roll it through a pasta machine, a strip at a time, into a long very thin sheet. Spread it with softened lard and roll it up tightly into a cylinder about 5 cm across, stretching each turn slightly. Coat the outside with lard, wrap and chill at least 30 minutes, ideally overnight.
For the filling, bring the milk to the boil with the lemon peel, remove the peel and whisk in the semolina. Cook 5 minutes, stirring, until thick, then cool.
Beat the ricotta with the sugar, yolk, cinnamon and orange blossom water, then stir in the cold semolina and the candied peel.

Bake at 400 °F (200 °C), fan, for 20 to 25 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
